name: NIAR Additive Manufacturing Techno-Economic Analysis cost model and TEA module (America Makes IMPACT project 5554.007)
year: 2023–2025 (period of performance Nov 14, 2023 to May 14, 2025; no final deliverable found publicly as of Oct 2026)
developer: Wichita State University National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR), VALDOS group (team listed in the briefing: Brady Williams, R. Andrulonis, M. Shaw, L. Tubesing, C. Combemale, P. Funk; no PI is labeled). Funded by OSD ManTech through AFRL agreement FA8650-20-2-5700 and administered by America Makes (project 5554.007; IMPACT Topic 8, Project 2).
description: A cost model for four metal AM modalities, plus a techno-economic analysis (TEA) module 'to be used by DoD personnel to aid in the decision of when to leverage AM'. The stated objective is to 'deliver a framework for when, where, and how to utilize metal AM technologies to bridge gaps in component sourcing.' The team compared 13 existing cost models and used advisory-board and government interviews to find omitted cost elements; the stated future work is to 'implement the gaps into a tool.' This update re-read the Jan 2024 interim briefing and searched for other NIAR tools built for the Air Force. None were found. NIAR's other Air Force work is B-1/F-16 digital twins, WAM materials data and scanning/reverse engineering. The ratings describe the planned cost structure in the interim briefing, not a verified final tool.
NRE_note: 'NRE (DFAM, engineering salary, etc.)' is listed only as a gap to add to the planned LPBF model and the cost-element matrix summarises published models, so whether the eventual tool uses NRE in its decision cannot be confirmed (NIAR interim briefing, Jan 2024).
Production_note: The four-modality cost model is a planned deliverable and the listed per-part elements (feedstock, build plate, machine cost, labour, energy, gas, build time, post-processing) summarise 13 published models, with no NIAR model, calculation or values shown (NIAR interim briefing, Jan 2024).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification appears only as 'supplier learning curve/common qualification', a maturation factor for the planned TEA module, so whether the tool will use qualification in its decision cannot be confirmed (NIAR interim briefing).
QA_Insp_note: 'Quality Control' is a row in the literature cost-element matrix and 'inspection rate per part application' is a gap to add to the planned LPBF model, so inspection is not shown in any built tool (NIAR interim briefing).
Storage_note: The advisory board named 'packaging and storage' among elements omitted from traditional models, to be considered in the planned TEA module, so whether the tool will use storage cannot be confirmed (NIAR interim briefing).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine depreciation appears in the literature cost-element matrix and a build-plate packing factor is a gap to add, but no NIAR model using machine capital is shown (NIAR interim briefing).
Shared_Capacity_note: The objective says 'when, where, and how', but the briefing has no capacity, utilisation or site content and no final tool, report or manuscript has been found (NIAR interim briefing; advocate's 2026 web search).
Speed_note: AOG, mission readiness and the cost of inoperable equipment are advisory-board items to consider in the planned TEA module, with no lead time used in any built tool (NIAR interim briefing).

name: Workbench for Additive Manufacturing Materials (WAM)
year: Unknown (first public description found: DoD ManTech JAMWG flyer, about Nov 2024)
developer: Wichita State University NIAR, under contract to the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC); overseen by the Joint AM Working Group
description: A database of metal AM material property data that DoD developed or licensed, shared across the services. NIAR builds and maintains it under an AFLCMC contract. It is a borderline entry, a data resource that supports material and process choice and qualification, not an analytical decision tool.
NRE_note: The flyer describes WAM only as shared metal AM property data and does not say whether it supports design or parameter development, and the portal is not public (JAMWG flyer).
Production_note: WAM is a database of metal AM material property data, so per-part production cost estimation is plainly outside its documented scope (JAMWG flyer).
QA_Qual_note: The flyer describes WAM only as shared metal AM property data and never mentions qualification or testing, and the 'bypass some of the material testing' quote in Manufacturing In Focus refers to NIAR's FAA shared materials database, not the DoD repository introduced in the next paragraph (JAMWG flyer; Manufacturing In Focus 2024).
QA_Insp_note: WAM is a shared database of material property data, so per-part inspection is plainly outside its documented scope (JAMWG flyer).
Storage_note: WAM is a shared database of material property data, so spare-part inventory is plainly outside its documented scope (JAMWG flyer).
Shared_Capital_note: The flyer describes WAM as a shared repository of DoD-developed or DoD-licensed metal AM property data reused across the services, a data resource that makes no decision and has no machine-capital content (JAMWG flyer).
Shared_Capacity_note: WAM is a shared database of material property data, so print capacity is plainly outside its documented scope (JAMWG flyer).
Speed_note: WAM is a shared database of material property data, so part lead time or availability is plainly outside its documented scope (JAMWG flyer).

name: Part Assessment and Cost Tool (PACT)
developer: US Air Force Rapid Sustainment Office (RSO) Advanced Manufacturing Program Office (AMPO), AFLCMC; contractor not named in public sources
description: A decision support application on Air Force Cloud One. It grades a supply chain part on 'supply chain impact', compatibility with or feasibility of advanced manufacturing, and return on investment (ROI), so SPOs can decide whether to start an advanced manufacturing project. AFLCMC describes it as performing 'cost-benefit analyses to determine ROI' for AM parts.
NRE_note: PACT 'assesses uploaded part files for their viability', but no source says whether reverse engineering, redesign or TDP cost enters the ROI grade (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com).
Production_note: PACT grades each candidate on 'return on investment' and the RSO-AdvM FAQ says it performs 'Cost-Benefit Analyses to determine ROIs for AM parts', but no cost inputs or elements are documented (AFLCMC news; AFLCMC RSO-AdvM FAQ).
QA_Qual_note: No source says whether qualification or airworthiness effort enters PACT's feasibility or ROI grades, and either could plausibly include it (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com).
QA_Insp_note: No source lists PACT's cost elements, so whether inspection is costed is not known (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com).
Storage_note: No source says whether the 'supply chain impact' grade covers inventory or obsolescence; the FAQ names obsolescence only as a reason AM is used in general (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com; RSO-AdvM FAQ).
Shared_Capital_note: No source says whether equipment investment or utilisation enters the ROI grade (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com).
Shared_Capacity_note: No source describes any capacity, utilisation or site analysis in PACT (AFLCMC news; 3DPrint.com).
Speed_note: Each part is graded on 'supply chain impact', a screening proxy for supply and availability problems, but lead time is not named and how the grade is built is not documented (AFLCMC news; RSO-AdvM FAQ).

name: SEEKR advanced manufacturing data analytics
year: Unknown (the session page is undated; it reports results from the RSO contract awarded in March 2023)
developer: EXPANSIA (SDVOSB), in partnership with the Air Force AMPO, under a Rapid Sustainment Office contract
description: Combines DoD logistics data with technical part data to prioritize part needs, flag parts affected by diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortages (DMSMS), and match part requirements to likely AM solutions. It reportedly assessed more than 6,000 Air Force parts and found about 900 viable for AM; under the RSO contract, 689 of 1,100 parts evaluated per airframe were found viable.
NRE_note: The session listing says SEEKR merges DoD logistics data with technical parts data but does not say whether data availability, reverse engineering or redesign effort is assessed, and no product documentation exists publicly (rapid3devent session page).
Production_note: Neither the session listing nor the contract press mentions part cost or any cost method, and only marketing-level descriptions exist (rapid3devent session page; ExecutiveGov 2023).
QA_Qual_note: Commercial airworthiness-certified printing processes are applied when developing the selected parts, but neither source shows certification or qualification used as a criterion in SEEKR's part selection, so whether the tool acts on qualification cannot be confirmed (rapid3devent session page; ExecutiveGov 2023).
QA_Insp_note: Neither the session listing nor the contract press mentions inspection or testing, and the tool's criteria are not public (rapid3devent session page; ExecutiveGov 2023).
Storage_note: SEEKR flags parts affected by DMSMS and material shortages as a screening criterion, with no inventory or holding-cost calculation (rapid3devent session page).
Shared_Capital_note: The contract press mentions part families and an organic capability roadmap, but no source says whether equipment investment or its sharing is assessed (ExecutiveGov 2023; rapid3devent session page).
Shared_Capacity_note: The contract aims to help build organic AM capability, but neither source says whether SEEKR considers capacity, site allocation or pooling (ExecutiveGov 2023; rapid3devent session page).
Speed_note: The session page claims SEEKR reduces lead time on obsolescence-affected parts but does not list lead time among the data it uses to prioritise parts, so whether the tool uses lead time in its decisions cannot be confirmed (rapid3devent session page).

name: DLA Legacy Parts AM Prescreening Tool (DLA prototype AM candidate selection tool)
developer: LMI with XSB Inc., Penn State (T. Simpson) and Virginia Tech (C. Williams), for the Defense Logistics Agency Weapon System Sustainment Program
description: A database query tool that narrows about 4.5 million DLA-managed parts to about 43,000 that fit an AM build envelope and exactly match a common AM feedstock, assuming no redesign. Users then filter by FSC, weapon system, criticality, lead time, unit cost, dimensions, material and machine, with engineering review of each candidate's technical data package (TDP) required before any decision. A 2019 Joint Force Quarterly article mentions a "limited Additive Part Candidate Identification Tool" from DLA Logistics Operations R&D, most likely this prototype.
NRE_note: TDP existence or availability is a logistics attribute and a Yes/No filter in the prototype, a proxy for reverse-engineering need, and every candidate goes to engineering review of the TDP; NRE is not costed and redesign is assumed away (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 2 and 4).
Production_note: Current unit price is a logistics attribute used only as a Cost range filter in the prototype; no AM production cost is computed (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 2 and 4).
QA_Qual_note: A criticality filter (critical safety item, flight safety critical part, SUBSAFE) narrows candidates, and QAP and first article test are listed as acceptance, test and qualification requirements to consider, but no qualification burden is estimated (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 2 and 4).
QA_Insp_note: Production lot testing is listed among the acceptance, test and qualification attributes to consider, but the prototype neither filters on nor costs it, so inspection does not enter the tool's screening (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 2).
Storage_note: Quantity on hand and demand are recorded part attributes and annual demand and backorder filters were only requested by users, so the prototype does not screen on stock or demand and has no inventory analysis (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 2-4).
Shared_Capital_note: The full report does not address printer purchase or capital investment; AM systems enter only through build envelope and feedstock, and the only cost question raised is who funds the decision-support process (LMI DL501T1, full text).
Shared_Capacity_note: The full report does not analyse production capacity or networks; AM building parts 'at or near the point of need' is mentioned only in passing and the only capacity-like constraint is build envelope (LMI DL501T1, full text).
Speed_note: Combined administrative plus production lead time from EBS is a Long Lead/Overage filter in day ranges, with backorder filters requested; lead time is not computed or valued (LMI DL501T1, Ch. 4).

name: NAVSEA AM part risk triage and TDP approval framework (with NAMPIE part identification events)
developer: Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA 05T, AM Technical Warrant Holder)
description: Parts are sorted into color-coded risk boxes: Yellow (under triage), Green (low criticality; can be approved at the waterfront or aboard ship), Blue (requires NAVSEA HQ review) and Red (cannot or should not be made by AM). Low-risk applications are delegated to local chief engineers, and others go through technical-authority approval that results in a TDP. NAMPIE events identify candidate shipboard parts, and a 'buy or print' Mission Impact Analysis uses the NAVSUP Price Fighter cost tool.
NRE_note: The approval route for parts outside the low-risk box ends in an approved TDP and NAMPIE events aim to influence technical data, but the TDP is a product of the process rather than an input to triage, and whether NRE enters the risk-box decision cannot be confirmed from the briefing (NRC briefing, Dec 2020).
Production_note: Integration of NAVSUP Price Fighter's AM cost-per-part tool into TDP development is under way and 'buy or print' decisions are a logistics-database goal, so whether the framework outputs or uses a part cost in its decisions cannot be confirmed from the briefing (NRC briefing, Dec 2020).
QA_Qual_note: The risk box is a criticality gate that sets the approval level (green: waterfront or shipboard; blue: NAVSEA HQ; red: not AM), with no class-specific test counts in the public material; DoD IG adds that parts are 'binned based on a risk, material, process maturity' (NRC briefing; DODIG-2020-003 p. 29).
QA_Insp_note: Neither the briefing nor the DoD IG audit mentions inspection or NDE in triage or TDP approval (the only testing named is off-gas testing of thermoplastics), and the internal criteria are not public (NRC briefing; DODIG-2020-003).
Storage_note: A parts repository is still being prototyped and entering AM parts into logistics databases for provisioning and 'buy or print' decisions is a goal, so whether the framework uses stock or inventory in its decisions cannot be confirmed (NRC briefing; DODIG-2020-003 p. 9 on JTDI).
Shared_Capital_note: The briefing mentions installing AM equipment on 8 platforms in 2019 but says nothing on equipment cost, amortisation or sharing, and the framework's internal criteria are not public (NRC briefing; DODIG-2020-003).
Shared_Capacity_note: Low-risk approvals are delegated to waterfront or ship chief engineers and a planned digital enclave would move manufacturing data between ship and shore, but the briefing does not say where parts are printed, so whether the framework routes print work across sites cannot be confirmed (NRC briefing).
Speed_note: Increasing readiness through 'production of obsolete or long-lead items' is a stated goal and a readiness logistics database is planned, but no lead-time criterion is given for NAMPIE or the risk boxes, so whether the framework uses lead time to decide cannot be confirmed (NRC briefing).

name: NAVAIR AM Candidate Assessment Tool (Navy STTR topic N23B-T032)
developer: Solicited by NAVAIR (transition targets: PEO-CS Digital Thread team and NAWCAD Lakehurst Digital Enterprise Tools Branch); no awardee found
description: A requested tool that uses expert-guided active machine learning on Technical Data Package and supply data (material, GD&T, acceptance criteria, criticality, demand, FSC) to screen out unsuitable parts, then estimate production cost and delivery schedule, building on an 'existing cost and time estimation tool' (possibly AMCAT; inference). The scores reflect the solicitation's requirements.
NRE_note: The topic draws inputs from the TDP (including data rights) but does not make reverse engineering, redesign or TDP creation a tool criterion or cost, and no delivered tool is public (Navy STTR N23B-T032 topic and Q&A).
Production_note: Phase I requires refining existing cost and time tools 'to predict production cost estimates' for AM candidates, a requirement for an undelivered tool, so whether a tool outputs or uses production cost cannot be confirmed from the solicitation (Navy STTR N23B-T032, Phase I).
QA_Qual_note: Criticality and acceptance criteria are named as TDP and supply-system data for screening out unsuitable parts, but they are requirements for an undelivered tool with no qualification steps specified, so use in a decision cannot be confirmed (Navy STTR N23B-T032, description and Q&A 5/26/23).
QA_Insp_note: Production cost estimates must consider post-processing including 'inspection' required to meet the part's acceptance criteria, a requirement for an undelivered tool, so whether inspection enters a tool's estimate cannot be confirmed (Navy STTR N23B-T032, Phase I).
Storage_note: The Q&A lists 'Demand' only among the fields the supply system 'commonly provides' and obsolescence is a stated motivation, but neither inventory nor demand is named as a screening criterion, and no delivered tool is public (Navy STTR N23B-T032, description and Q&A 5/26 and 5/30/23).
Shared_Capital_note: The topic mentions 'existing additive manufacturing systems of interest' only as envelope limits for screening, not machine investment or utilisation, and no delivered tool is public (Navy STTR N23B-T032, Phase I).
Shared_Capacity_note: The topic and Q&A do not mention capacity, utilisation or multiple sites, and no delivered tool is public (Navy STTR N23B-T032).
Speed_note: Predicting AM 'delivery schedules' is a Phase I requirement and reducing 'long lead times' is a stated aim, but no delivered tool exists, so whether lead time is computed or used cannot be confirmed (Navy STTR N23B-T032).

name: Joint Additive Manufacturing Model Exchange (JAMMEX)
developer: Defense Logistics Agency and America Makes; development overseen by the Joint AM Working Group
description: A secure web repository for storing, managing and sharing 3D AM models, cold spray procedures and metadata across the services and DLA. It is an enabling digital-inventory system, not an analytical decision tool.
NRE_note: The DoD IG says one system for sharing approved AM technical data 'could eliminate duplicative AM efforts', a claimed saving from stored design files; public sources do not show the repository using engineering effort in any decision (DoD IG DODIG-2020-003, pp. i, 16, 18).
Production_note: DLA says parts printed through JAMMEX 'would have otherwise cost more' and that it can 'decrease costs', a cost claim; public sources show no per-part cost used or output by the repository (DLA news 2020).
QA_Qual_note: DLA makes sure 'models that go on JAMMEX are approved models' and the DoD IG says it shares approved data, an approval gate on what enters the repository, with no qualification effort or cost (DLA news 2020; DoD IG DODIG-2020-003, p. 16).
QA_Insp_note: The flyer, DoD IG audit and both DLA articles describe stored models, cold-spray procedures and metadata but none says whether test or acceptance requirements are included, and the CAC-only portal cannot be opened (JAMWG flyer 2024; DoD IG; DLA news 2020, 2023).
Storage_note: DLA says JAMMEX provides 'a catalog of alternate sources for hard-to-procure and obsolete parts', a digital-inventory feature; public sources do not show the repository using stock or obsolescence to decide anything (DLA news 2023; DLA news 2020).
Shared_Capital_note: The DoD IG describes JAMMEX as a way for services to 'share approved AM technical data' and 'view and use each other's technical data', reuse of approval work offered as a feature; public sources show no reuse or capital factor entering a decision, and machine capital is not addressed (DoD IG DODIG-2020-003, pp. 16, 18).
Shared_Capacity_note: JAMMEX's documented scope is to store, manage and share models, cold-spray procedures and metadata, and DLA says only that users 'download and print models' through it; no source describes pooling or redirecting printer capacity (JAMWG flyer 2024; DLA news 2020).
Speed_note: DLA claims JAMMEX parts would otherwise have 'taken longer to procure' and that it can 'improve responsiveness', time benefits claimed; whether the repository uses lead time in any decision cannot be confirmed from public sources (DLA news 2020 and 2023).

name: Techno-Economic Analysis of Powder Bed Fusion for the Air Force (IMPACT Topic 9)
developer: Wohlers Associates (ASTM International); IMPACT call funded by OSD(R&E) ManTech and AFRL via America Makes/NCDMM
description: A landscape assessment and interviews with industry and DoD, leading to a final report that prioritizes investment areas to 'improve the business case and reduce part costs' for metal PBF. No cost model is described publicly.
NRE_note: Press releases and the project workshop page describe expert interviews and recommendations to lower $/cm3, but none says whether design, redesign or parameter-development effort is analysed, and no report is public (ASTM AM CoE workshop page; Metal AM 2023).
Production_note: The analysis aims to 'improve the business case and reduce part costs' through a landscape assessment, interviews and process-improvement simulations aimed at the lowest $/cm3, but no cost model is public, so whether it computes or ranks on part cost cannot be confirmed (Metal AM 2023; ASTM AM CoE workshop page).
QA_Qual_note: 'Understanding / Use of Part Classification' and qualification of multi-laser systems are listed workshop topics, so qualification is discussed, but whether the analysis uses it in its prioritisation cannot be confirmed from public sources (ASTM AM CoE 5th Specialty Workshop page).
QA_Insp_note: 'Using In-Situ Monitoring to reduce cost' is a listed topic of the Topic 9 survey follow-up, discussion of inspection as a cost lever, but whether the analysis uses inspection in its prioritisation cannot be confirmed from public sources (ASTM AM CoE workshop page).
Storage_note: The press releases and workshop page mention a sustainment breakout but not inventory, stock or spares, and the final report is not public (ASTM AM CoE workshop page; Metal AM 2023).
Shared_Capital_note: 'Automation for lights-out operation Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)' is a listed topic, discussion of machine utilisation, but whether the analysis uses machine capital or utilisation in its prioritisation cannot be confirmed from public sources (ASTM AM CoE workshop page).
Shared_Capacity_note: The only related topic concerns the health of the contract manufacturing base, and no source says whether pooled print capacity or its effect on lead time is analysed (ASTM AM CoE workshop page).
Speed_note: No press release or the workshop page mentions lead time, availability or readiness, and the final report is not public (Metal AM 2023; 3DPrint.com 2023; ASTM AM CoE workshop page).

name: Casting & Forging Techno-Economic Framework (IMPACT Topic 8, Project 1)
developer: Deloitte Consulting LLP; IMPACT call funded by OSD(R&E) ManTech and AFRL via America Makes/NCDMM
description: Listed only by title as an IMPACT Topic 8 award to 'bridge component sourcing gaps with AM parts for casting and forging applications'. No content was found.
NRE_note: Only the title, lead (Deloitte, no partners) and the one-line Topic 8 description are public, and none says whether design, reverse-engineering or parameter-development effort is analysed (NCDMM award and call pages; Modern Casting Jan 2024).
Production_note: 'Techno-economic' in the title and topic implies cost analysis but the method and whether per-part AM cost is built up are not described anywhere public (NCDMM award and call pages).
QA_Qual_note: Manufacturing readiness assessment is in the topic text, but whether qualification cost or effort is treated cannot be established from title-level sources (NCDMM call page).
QA_Insp_note: No public source describes the framework's content, so inspection treatment cannot be established (NCDMM award and call pages).
Storage_note: No public source describes the framework's content, so whether inventory effects are analysed cannot be established (NCDMM award and call pages).
Shared_Capital_note: No public source describes the framework's content, so equipment investment or utilisation treatment cannot be established (NCDMM award and call pages).
Shared_Capacity_note: No public source describes the framework's content, so shared or pooled capacity treatment cannot be established (NCDMM award and call pages).
Speed_note: The call section heading is 'Demonstrating Lead Time, Productivity, and Yield Improvements', but that is the call's aim, not a documented feature of the Deloitte framework, so its lead-time treatment is not established (NCDMM call page).

name: Selection of Additive Manufacturing Equipment (AMRDEC TR-RDMR-WD-16-87)
developer: US Army AMRDEC Weapons Development and Integration Directorate (L. Hall)
description: A narrative justification for choosing three AM machine types based on capability gaps from a workforce survey, part size and complexity (DED for large near-net parts, PBF for small complex parts), functional integration, and input from other labs. There is no scoring or cost model.
NRE_note: Process and material characterization at AMRDEC and topology optimisation are discussed as planned work, but NRE is not a factor in the machine-selection justification (DTIC AD1031372, pp. 5, 7).
Production_note: Fabrication cost is discussed in words, with one narrative figure of $10K-$50K of reusable powder for a first powder-bed build, but cost is not a criterion in choosing the machines (DTIC AD1031372, pp. 1, 6).
QA_Qual_note: In-house material characterization, locked-down parameters and current systems' inability to make structural test components are discussed as background, but qualification is not a factor in the machine-selection justification (DTIC AD1031372, pp. 1, 5, 8).
QA_Insp_note: Full report read: metrology and vision devices appear only as features of the multifunctional printer, and no part inspection, NDE, CT or acceptance testing is specified (DTIC AD1031372).
Storage_note: Full report read: repair of worn aviation parts is mentioned, but there is no spare-part inventory, stock or obsolescence content (DTIC AD1031372, p. 5).
Shared_Capital_note: The report says the machines will 'serve AMRDEC as a whole' across user groups, a stated purpose rather than a criterion, and no machine cost is spread across users or used to decide (DTIC AD1031372, Introduction, Sec. III).
Shared_Capacity_note: Full report read: capacity appears only as build-envelope size, and no pooling of print capacity across sites or users, or effect on lead time, is discussed (DTIC AD1031372, pp. 2, 6).
Speed_note: Decreased fabrication time and quick blown-powder deposition are claimed as AM benefits, but no build or lead time is a criterion in the selection (DTIC AD1031372, pp. 1, 3).

name: Techno-economic performance metrics for large-format metal DED (ORNL MDF)
developer: Oak Ridge National Laboratory Manufacturing Demonstration Facility (A. G. Stevens, P. Mhatre, L. Heinrich, C. Masuo, A. Shanafield, T. Feldhausen, B. K. Post)
description: Techno-economic and life-cycle metrics (build rate, volume, resolution, feedstock cost, embodied energy and CO2e) for several large-format DED processes, compared with conventional manufacturing. It is a set of comparison metrics, not a decision tool.
NRE_note: The abstract does not mention design or engineering effort, and no proceedings paper was found in searches or in the lead author's ORNL publication list (SFF 2024 abstract; ORNL profile).
Production_note: Feedstock cost and build rate are presented as technoeconomic (manufacturing cost) metrics for each DED process against conventional routes, but no per-part cost build-up is described (SFF 2024 abstract).
QA_Qual_note: The abstract does not mention qualification, and no full paper was found (SFF 2024 abstract; ORNL profile).
QA_Insp_note: The abstract does not mention inspection; 'resolution' is a process metric, not inspection, and no full paper was found (SFF 2024 abstract).
Storage_note: The abstract does not mention inventory, and no full paper was found (SFF 2024 abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The abstract lists build-rate, feedstock-cost and energy metrics but not equipment capital; the 2026 Shanafield and Stevens DED cost model is a separate paper and does not settle this one (SFF 2024 abstract; ORNL profile).
Shared_Capacity_note: The abstract does not mention capacity sharing, and no full paper was found (SFF 2024 abstract).
Speed_note: Build rate is presented as a quantified metric for each large-format DED process and compared with conventional processes, which puts a number on production speed only; time to part, lead time or availability is not described (SFF 2024 abstract).

name: Project TAMPA additive manufacturing accelerator (spiral-based part adoption)
developer: UK MOD Defence Support / UK Strategic Command with DE&S; industry framework: Babcock, NP Aerospace, RBSL, Thales, AMFG
description: Accelerator that sequences parts in spirals by safety criticality and material (spiral 1: 11 non-safety-critical metallic NSN parts; spiral 2: safety-critical metallic parts) and takes successful parts to a DE&S recommendation for adoption into the defence inventory.
NRE_note: 'Intellectual Property or Design Rights' is named as one of four problem areas and a final phase for parts needing design-rights access is described as planned, while the spirals are defined by safety criticality and material, so whether the programme uses design-data availability to decide which parts it takes on cannot be confirmed from public sources (fw-mag; Operations Engineer July 2023, p. 15).
Production_note: MOD sources claim 'significant cost savings' and the 2026 article mentions 'cost efficiencies'; whether the accelerator uses part cost in selecting or recommending parts cannot be confirmed from public sources (DE&S news page; Eureka; TCT 2026 via pulse.bot).
QA_Qual_note: Spirals are sequenced by safety criticality, 'certification and qualification of parts' is one of four problem areas, safety-critical parts are 'certified by the producer', and successful parts get a DE&S adoption recommendation, all without qualification counts or costs (DE&S news page; fw-mag; Operations Engineer July 2023).
QA_Insp_note: No TAMPA source names per-part inspection or testing: the X-ray and porosity remarks in Operations Engineer follow the words 'Separate to Project TAMPA' and concern a Type 22 naval gun part, and the 2026 Mastiff article mentions only 'reliability and traceability standards' (Operations Engineer July 2023, p. 15; TCT 2026 via pulse.bot; DE&S; fw-mag).
Storage_note: 'Reduction of the need to stockpile' is claimed as a benefit and inventory management is named as a problem area; whether the accelerator uses stock or demand in selecting parts cannot be confirmed from public sources (DE&S news page; fw-mag).
Shared_Capital_note: MOD news, Babcock news and trade press describe the programme but none says whether machine investment or sharing is assessed, and the method is unpublished (DE&S; Eureka; Babcock 2024).
Shared_Capacity_note: The MOD vision of 'a series of global hubs' and a 2024 demonstration sending print files to a remote machine describe distributed printing, but whether the programme assigns or routes work across printers cannot be confirmed from public sources (DE&S news page; Babcock news 2024).
Speed_note: A periscope clamp made in 'days instead of months' and an estimated 60% faster Mastiff turnaround are quoted case results; whether the accelerator uses lead time in selecting parts cannot be confirmed from public sources (Eureka; TCT 2026 via pulse.bot).

name: AM in military logistics assessment for the Finnish Defence Forces and Millog (SWOT/AHP and depot-placement recommendation)
developer: Finnish National Defence University (S. Rautio, doctoral thesis 2023); journal article by I. Valtonen, S. Rautio and M. Salmi, 'Capability Development in Hybrid Organizations - Enhancing Military Logistics with Additive Manufacturing', Progress in Additive Manufacturing 7 (2022) 1037-1052 (authors confirmed by the thesis record, which lists it as one of the four constituent articles)
description: Integrative review, case study, SWOT and AHP with experts (journal article) on how AM fits the FDF-Millog hybrid maintenance model; the thesis concludes industrial AM is best placed in repair-depot maintenance or for civilian components.
NRE_note: The article notes that printing needs a 3D CAD model and that configuration management should hold baseline design data, but this is discussion and design or digitisation effort enters no decision (Valtonen, Rautio & Salmi 2022, Secs. 2.5, 3.3).
Production_note: The commercial partner's business case and payback are discussed in words and 'cost and investment of initial implementation' is a weighted SWOT weakness, but the weights drive no ranking or recommendation and no per-part cost enters a decision (Valtonen et al. 2022, Secs. 1, 3.2, Table 3).
QA_Qual_note: Quality issues and incomplete material and design knowledge are listed as barriers to AM spares, and no qualification step or criterion is used to decide anything (Valtonen et al. 2022, Secs. 1, 2.5).
QA_Insp_note: The article remarks that coordinate measuring machines are still needed at some stage of printing, but inspection enters no assessment or decision (Valtonen et al. 2022, Sec. 3.4).
Storage_note: A decentralised model is said to reduce the supply chain 'to merely a supply of raw materials such as powder and wire', a claim that the assessment does not use in any decision (Valtonen et al. 2022, Sec. 2.5).
Shared_Capital_note: Cited printer prices (EOS M 100 at about EUR 300k) and a payback of decades with one customer are discussion, and the weighted SWOT opportunity on investment savings from existing capabilities drives no output, so capital sharing enters no decision (Valtonen et al. 2022, Sec. 3.4, Table 3).
Shared_Capacity_note: Centralised and distributed printing are compared in discussion (lower utilisation but more resilience when decentralised) and the depot placement in the thesis is the authors' conclusion, not a rule that uses capacity to decide (Valtonen et al. 2022, Sec. 2.5; Rautio thesis abstract, Doria).
Speed_note: Responsiveness is emphasised and waiting time is said to be no more than machine cycle time plus post-processing, qualification and assembly, but no lead time enters the assessment and the weighted SWOT item on system availability drives no decision (Valtonen et al. 2022, Sec. 3.1, Tables 2-3).

name: FFI field AM trial assessment and component-suitability analysis (Norwegian Armed Forces)
developer: Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI) with Norwegian Special Forces (NORSOF)
description: Report on a containerised 3D printing capability at exercise Cold Response 2016; it references a prior FFI analysis of which components suit AM (Norberg and Oestereng, not located) and sketches distributed vs centralised production.
NRE_note: Recommends a spare-parts database with linked CAD files, strength analyses for critical components and printer-specific parameter sets, but the report applies no NRE criterion in any decision (FFI 16/01008 full text).
Production_note: The full report's only cost figures are the containerised capability's set-up cost (about NOK 800,000, of which NOK 450,000 for the printer), which is capital, and it gives no per-part, material or price figure or AM-versus-conventional cost comparison (FFI 16/01008 full text).
QA_Qual_note: States that AM parts will require testing, standardisation and certification and a quality-assured production process, as discussion, with no qualification step in any decision (FFI 16/01008 full text).
QA_Insp_note: The full report states the trial parts were not tested but judged fully usable and sets no per-part inspection step; its testing call concerns material qualification and certification (FFI 16/01008 full text).
Storage_note: Argues AM can reduce inventory and transport needs, a claimed benefit that the report does not use in any decision (FFI 16/01008 full text).
Shared_Capital_note: Gives the printer's purchase cost (NOK 450,000 of NOK 800,000) as a trial figure and sketches distributed or centralised production, but machine cost is not spread over parts or users or used in any decision (FFI 16/01008, Ch. 2 and 4.3).
Shared_Capacity_note: Sketches producing spares near the user versus centrally and reports a titanium part made by an external firm from transmitted files, as description, with no rule for assigning work to sites (FFI 16/01008 full text).
Speed_note: Reports quick field fixes as trial results, such as a FLIR camera spacer designed and printed within 30 minutes so a boat could deploy, but lead time is not used in any decision (FFI 16/01008 full text).

name: AM-powered aircraft logistic support business model (Leonardo Aircraft Division)
developer: Politecnico di Torino (G. Viano, MSc thesis) with Leonardo S.p.A. Aircraft Division
description: Cost and business model for an AM-based logistic support service with fixed, variable, compliance/certification and per-client costs under a performance-based fixed-fee SLA; uses criticality, make/buy and obsolescence data as selection inputs.
NRE_note: One-time engineering is an explicit cost term in the service cost study: starting costs for candidate selection (fixed assessment times and a success rate), redesign and validation (fixed times plus margin), procedure development and catalogue development, with values withheld as confidential (PoliTo thesis 6.5.1, 6.7.1).
Production_note: The cost study has production cost terms (material from the maximum printable material per job plus a transport and wastage margin, and five-year linear hardware depreciation), but values are withheld and no per-part cost is built up (PoliTo thesis 6.7.2, 6.7.4).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is an explicit cost element: procedure development with destructive and non-destructive testing is a starting cost, per-client system qualification and integration is a one-time cost, and compliance and certification is its own cost category, with values withheld (PoliTo thesis 6.5.3, 6.7.1, 6.7.3).
QA_Insp_note: Radiography, tomography and destructive testing of every PBF part (visual, radiography and tensile samples for FFF) are described as part of the service, but no inspection cost or count enters the cost study or any decision (PoliTo thesis 5.3.1-5.3.2, 6.5.3).
Storage_note: Inventory reduction is argued in words and warehousing appears only as a raw-material logistics cost, while part selection uses technical, logistical and economic criteria and obsolescence appears only in the existing technical-vetting process, so stock does not enter the cost model or any decision (PoliTo thesis 2.5.1, 6.4.1, 6.5.2, 7.1.1).
Shared_Capital_note: Internal and per-client hardware is depreciated straight-line over five years and set against costs in a breakeven around year 3-4, but no utilisation, parts-per-machine or cross-client allocation is used (PoliTo thesis 6.7.1-6.7.5).
Shared_Capacity_note: Leonardo-owned hubs and a network of qualified suppliers owning AM resources are described as the service concept, but no capacity, pooling or work assignment enters the model (PoliTo thesis 5.3.2-5.3.3).
Speed_note: Costly AOG downtime and SLA availability and delivery-time commitments are discussed without figures, and lead time, downtime and availability do not enter the cost model or any decision (PoliTo thesis 6.2, 6.6.2).

name: Deutsche Bahn AM part identification and business-case process (with 3YOURMIND AM Part Identifier)
developer: Deutsche Bahn AM team; vendor platform 3YOURMIND (Agile PLM, AM Part Identifier)
description: Combines bottom-up idea submission from ~200,000 employees and top-down automated scanning of inventory/stock lists (AMPI and AI) to flag candidates, then prioritised assessment and per-part business cases. Reported results: 74% faster assessments and 50-70% savings vs conventional procurement.
NRE_note: DB lacked CAD data and has parts reconstructed from 3D scans and re-engineered (gear housing), but no public source shows CAD availability or engineering effort used in AMPI screening or the per-part business case (DB 3D printing page; EOS blog 2025).
Production_note: Per-part business cases compare AM with conventional procurement and report 50-70% savings, but the cost method and inputs are not disclosed (casestudies.com 3YOURMIND case).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification and testing are named as the main bottleneck and DB/MGA worked on a site-capability standard (cited as DIN 52920), but the 'qualification' that ideas go to experts for is the experts' per-part assessment, and whether qualification enters the assessment cannot be confirmed from public sources (EOS blog 2025; Automation Alley report).
QA_Insp_note: DB says every printed component undergoes extensive testing before use (fatigue strength cited), but whether testing scope or cost enters part selection or the business case cannot be confirmed from public sources (DB 3D printing page; EOS blog 2025).
Storage_note: AMPI scans inventory and stock lists to flag candidates and the EUR 1.8bn warehouse and avoided minimum order quantities are cited as savings, but no source says stock levels or holding cost are AMPI criteria or business-case inputs (Automation Alley report; casestudies.com; EOS blog 2025).
Shared_Capital_note: Sources mention DB's own industrial printers in Nuremberg and Neumuenster but none says whether machine investment or its spread across parts enters the assessment (DB page; casestudies.com; Automation Alley; EOS blog).
Shared_Capacity_note: DB prints in its own works, also uses external providers and founded the Mobility goes Additive network of over 150 firms, but no source shows the process assigning or routing work across sites or printers (DB 3D printing page; EOS blog 2025).
Speed_note: Shorter lead times and avoided train standstills are cited as savings and cases are quoted (gear housing two-year quote vs two months; roll-stop 10 to 5 months), but these are reported outcomes and no source shows lead time or downtime entering AMPI screening or the business case (EOS blog 2025; Automation Alley report).

name: MPA/NAMIC/SSA maritime AM Joint Industry Programme part screening (Phase 1)
developer: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore, NAMIC, Singapore Shipping Association; DNV GL lead research performer; 10 SSA members incl. Wilhelmsen; collaborators Waertsilae, Sembcorp Marine, SpareParts3D, Ivaldi
description: Four-stage screening of ~600,000 part-order lines using a scoring matrix of commercial drivers (unit cost, quantity, lead time), AM supply chain benefits (lead-time reduction, stockyard inventory, TCO) and technical aspects; shortlisted 100 parts in three feasibility categories.
NRE_note: 'Potential opportunities to improve functionality or reduce complexity with better design' is a scoring-matrix criterion, so redesign potential enters the ranking, while drawings are used only to identify parts and no one-time engineering cost is computed (MPA public report, pp. 17-19).
Production_note: Unit purchase cost (SGD/unit) is a scoring-matrix criterion and cost saving is defined as conventional minus AM cost over named elements, but no per-part build-up or weights are given and case savings are quoted without method (MPA public report, pp. 18-19, 38-39).
QA_Qual_note: Shortlisted parts are sorted into feasible-with or feasible-without class certification on assumed safety criticality, and certification is named as an AM cost element, with no costed qualification activity (MPA public report, pp. 5, 18, 26).
QA_Insp_note: Parts evaluation is listed among AM cost elements in the cost-saving definition, destructive or non-destructive evaluation is discussed as a confidence factor and a quality control plan is drafted for categorised parts, but inspection is not a scoring criterion or screening factor (MPA public report, pp. 13, 16, 18-19).
Storage_note: Potential to reduce stockyard inventory is a scored benefit criterion, but no holding cost or stock level is calculated (MPA public report, p. 19).
Shared_Capital_note: Upfront machine and facility capex is called considerable and partnering with a third-party AM company or forming a consortium is suggested, with ROI and TCO discussed, but machine capital and its sharing are not used in the screening (MPA public report, pp. 13, 29).
Shared_Capacity_note: Distributed printer networks, ship and port printing and AM service-provider networks are described, but they do not enter the screening and no work is assigned across sites (MPA public report, pp. 7, 29, 36, 38).
Speed_note: Lead time for delivery and potential to reduce procurement lead time are scoring-matrix criteria and a partner case quotes under 72 h versus up to 12 weeks, but lead time is not computed (MPA public report, pp. 19, 38).

name: Wilhelmsen DAVAMS on-demand spare part service model and Digital Asset Review Tool (DART)
developer: Wilhelmsen Ships Service (lead) with Ivaldi Group, Pelagus 3D and SINTEF; demo parts from Valland, Kongsberg Maritime, Kawasaki Heavy Industries
decision_levels: Part selection; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
earlier_versions: Wilhelmsen Early Adopter Program (2019): first on-demand 3D-printed spare parts service for ship operators, with parts passing a digitisation and certification process and starting with parts not needing class approval; DART was added later under DAVAMS (2022-2026).
description: Service model for local on-demand production of genuine OEM spares with a part identification and feasibility step, DART (automatic GHG, cost and lead-time estimates for AM vs conventional, designed for sparse data), and a cloud digital warehouse holding design files, qualification rules and inspection records.
NRE_note: Parts pass a 'digitization and certification process' and a part identification and feasibility step before production, but whether digitisation or redesign effort enters any decision of the service or DART cannot be confirmed from public sources (Maritime Executive 2019; Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary).
Production_note: DART, which the project reports as developed, provides automated cost assessments for AM vs conventional manufacturing, but the project summary documents no inputs or method (Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary).
QA_Qual_note: The digital warehouse stores qualification requirements and one early adopter (Executive Ship Management) planned to start with parts not needing class approval, but whether the service uses qualification to decide which parts are produced cannot be confirmed from public sources (Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary; Maritime Executive 2019).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection information is stored in the digital warehouse and the demonstrator chain included testing, but whether inspection enters any decision of the service or DART cannot be confirmed from public sources (Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary).
Storage_note: The service is claimed to eliminate 'the need for physical inventory storage' with lower inventory costs; whether the service or DART uses stock or demand in its decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (Maritime Executive 2019).
Shared_Capital_note: The project summary and 2019 press do not mention printer investment or sharing among subscribers, and no DART documentation is public (Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary; Maritime Executive 2019).
Shared_Capacity_note: Local micro-factories and partner tech centres (Singapore, Muelheim) are described as a network supplying subscribing vessels; whether the service assigns or routes work across these sites cannot be confirmed from public sources (Maritime Executive 2019; 3DPrint.com 2019).
Speed_note: DART, which the project reports as developed, provides automated lead-time assessments for AM vs conventional manufacturing 'even where detailed data is limited', but no inputs, method or outputs are documented (Prosjektbanken DAVAMS summary).

name: DNV Digital Warehouse JIP quality-assurance framework for distributed on-demand spare parts
developer: DNV with 18 JIP companies (incl. Saudi Aramco, ConocoPhillips, Vallourec, Ramlab, Norsk Titanium, Immensa, 3YOURMIND); DNV AM Energy group
description: JIP to create a quality-assurance framework for distributed, on-demand printing of spare parts close to where they are needed; DNV also developed a digital-inventory standard with Immensa and the AM qualification standard DNV-ST-B203.
NRE_note: The JIP pages and 3YOURMIND's account mention part identification but not digitisation or redesign effort; DNV-RP-B205 (2025) covers digitising parts but neither its landing page nor TCT's report links it to this JIP (DNV JIP pages; RP-B205 page; TCT).
Production_note: Connected AM manufacturers supply price and lead time to the 3YOURMIND platform used in the JIP's ecosystem simulation, but the price is the supplier's and whether the JIP's framework uses per-part cost in any decision is not public (3YOURMIND news on the DNV JIP, 2021).
QA_Qual_note: The JIP's ecosystem simulation runs an algorithm-based part assessment of suitable AM use cases whose inputs include part requirements, materials and qualifications, but no qualification steps or costs are public (3YOURMIND news on the DNV JIP, 2021; DNV JIP pages).
QA_Insp_note: Neither the DNV JIP pages nor partner news say whether per-part inspection or testing is covered, and no deliverable is public (DNV JIP pages; 3YOURMIND news).
Storage_note: The JIP is motivated by stocked spares that are never used, tie up value and incur warehouse upkeep, and whether the framework uses stock in its decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (DNV JIP pages).
Shared_Capital_note: The JIP pages mention only the minimal set-up needed to print a new part, not machine investment or sharing, and no deliverable is public (DNV JIP pages).
Shared_Capacity_note: The premise is distributed printing from cloud-sent files close to operations, and the simulation platform lets end users dispatch orders to connected AM manufacturers, but whether the framework assigns work among sites cannot be confirmed from public sources (DNV JIP pages; 3YOURMIND news 2021).
Speed_note: Long lead times are the stated motivation and connected manufacturers supply lead times to the simulation platform, but whether lead time is used in any selection cannot be confirmed from public sources (DNV JIP pages; 3YOURMIND news 2021).

name: Equinor digital inventory / Digital Supply Network programme
developer: Equinor with TotalEnergies, Shell, ConocoPhillips, Vaar Energi and Fieldnode (Fieldmade spin-off); separate Siemens Energy-Equinor-Fieldmade JIP
description: Programme to replace physical inventory (about EUR 2.5bn) with digital files printed near point of use, targeting 25% inventory reduction in five years and 50% in ten; no part screening method is published.
NRE_note: Recreating obsolete parts relies on 3D scanning and modelling and OEMs upload 3D-model recipes, activities the programme performs; no screening method is published, so whether engineering effort enters any decision cannot be confirmed (Equinor magazine; Valve World).
Production_note: Cost appears only as claimed case savings (plastic screws said to save USD 10M) and LCA comparisons with conventional supply; no screening method is published, so whether part cost enters any decision cannot be confirmed (Equinor magazine; Valve World).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is discussed as a requirement and barrier (sector applications normally need qualification and certification, DNV joined the flange work), but no published method uses it as a gate or factor, so its role in decisions cannot be confirmed (Formnext fonmag; Valve World; Equinor magazine).
QA_Insp_note: The press and magazine articles mention only a polymer replica to check a 3D model and error-free robotic welds, not inspection or testing of printed spares, and no programme procedure is public (Equinor magazine; Valve World; Seatrade).
Storage_note: Inventory cuts of 25% in five years and 50% in ten on a ~EUR 2.5-3bn stock said to be 80% unused are programme goals, not inputs to a published method, so whether stock enters part selection cannot be confirmed (Formnext fonmag; Valve World).
Shared_Capital_note: The articles say a mobile microfactory was hired from Fieldmade to build competence across Equinor, Aker Solutions and suppliers, but none discusses machine investment or how it is spread (Equinor magazine; Valve World).
Shared_Capacity_note: A multi-operator Digital Supply Network with OEM recipes, service-provider printing near the point of use and planned hubs in Hammerfest, Helgeland and Bergen is described as a concept; no published method routes work across it (Valve World; Equinor magazine).
Speed_note: Lead-time cuts are quoted from cases or as goals (a flange from 40 to 10 weeks; 3-6 months down to 4 weeks); no method is published, so whether lead time enters any decision cannot be confirmed (Equinor magazine; Valve World).

name: Shell digital inventory and AM supplier qualification approach
developer: Shell with Baker Hughes and other suppliers
description: Shell defines digital part documentation with suppliers and a repeatable qualification process for AM spare part vendors so parts can be bought on demand; first case was AM impellers for a seven-stage centrifugal pump made by Baker Hughes.
NRE_note: When no qualified OEM is available Shell reverse-engineers the part and has a commercial supplier print it from a 3D model, so OEM availability decides the reverse-engineering route, and Shell defines each part's digital documentation with suppliers, but this effort is not costed (The Fabricator; Metal AM 2022).
Production_note: Lower spare-part cost is claimed in words; whether the approach uses production cost in any decision cannot be confirmed from public sources (The Fabricator).
QA_Qual_note: Shell buys AM spares from suppliers it has qualified to supply them (Baker Hughes' Talamona facility was qualified to supply its assets) and aims for a repeatable vendor qualification process, but no steps, test sets or costs are given (Metal AM 2022; The Fabricator).
QA_Insp_note: The first impellers underwent intensive pre-installation testing to be accepted for operation, a step reported for this case; whether the approach requires inspection as a gate cannot be confirmed from press sources (Metal AM 2022; The Fabricator).
Storage_note: A saving of about $100,000 per stocked pump from not holding parts is a claimed estimate; whether the approach uses stock or holding cost in any decision cannot be confirmed from public sources (Metal AM 2022).
Shared_Capital_note: Press mentions Shell's roughly 15 polymer, ceramic and metal printers but says nothing on how machine investment is weighed or shared, and only press describes the approach (The Fabricator).
Shared_Capacity_note: Shell's stated approach routes parts to qualified OEMs, to commercial suppliers printing reverse-engineered models when no OEM is available and to in-house printing for emergencies, with no capacity or lead-time model (The Fabricator).
Speed_note: In emergencies, and when IP is not an issue, Shell prints spare parts in-house rather than through outside suppliers, so urgency acts as a routing gate, while the 40-day print, heat-treat and test cycle (85% under normal delivery) is a quoted case result, not an output of the approach (The Fabricator).

name: Onboard metal AM implementation roadmap and part filter (Heerema Marine Contractors)
developer: TU Delft (M.J. Kolthof, MSc thesis) with Heerema Marine Contractors; vendor partner Layertec
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Phased roadmap (research, plastic then metal printing, opportunities) for onboard AM with part filters (geometry, vendor check, application check, cost comparison) and a Harris-profile evaluation; quantifies machine investment, inventory and downtime context.
NRE_note: Modelling parts is noted to cost man-hours and CAD availability is listed only as a qualitative 'printing variable' in a minimum-maximum delivery-time indication, but neither CAD availability nor modelling effort is a criterion in the part filters or the cost comparison (TU Delft thesis pp. 30, 43, 58-59).
Production_note: The final filter step compares cost using vendor per-part cases (CNC $980 vs Studio System $148), and a costs overview computes some running-cost terms per sinter run (65 kWh x EUR 0.17 = EUR 11.05; gas), but no full per-part AM cost is built up (TU Delft thesis p. 58 Table 5, App. 36).
QA_Qual_note: Criticality and the need to certify are a deciding filter, external certification by Lloyd's or DNV is required for critical parts and the Chief Engineer approves prints, used as gates without costing (TU Delft thesis p. 23, App. 26, p. 78).
QA_Insp_note: Lloyd's advises NDT followed by lab tests and the author ran tensile (two samples per part) and hardness tests as research, but the roadmap does not require inspection before a printed part is used or use it in any decision (TU Delft thesis pp. 51-55, 69).
Storage_note: Uses the ~USD 13M on-board stock value in a calculation (a 5% cut saves ~USD 650k; a 1.8% cut equals the printer investment), an assumed reduction rather than a modelled effect on stock or holding cost (TU Delft thesis p. 57, p. 74).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine investment (Studio System ~EUR 220k, Ultimaker S5 EUR 6k) is entered and set against one vessel's stock value (about 1.74%), with one printer per vessel assumed and no utilisation or sharing across vessels modelled (TU Delft thesis p. 57, App. 19).
Shared_Capacity_note: Printing on other vessels and an onshore factory warehouse (Desktop Metal Production System) making parts for the fleet are long-term opportunities in the roadmap, which does not assign or route work among vessels or sites (TU Delft thesis pp. 36, 65).
Speed_note: Reports production time for the metal route (38 h debind plus 44 h sinter) as a design rule, a partial time model, while downtime (~USD 1M/day) and delivery times of up to 4-5 months are context and lead time is not computed per part (TU Delft thesis p. 44 Design Rule 5, p. 17, App. 4).

name: AMDSP 2.0 AM cost and lead-time calculator
developer: Aalto University (within the VTT/Aalto digital spare parts projects)
earlier_versions: AMDSP first version (DIVA project, c. 2018): MATLAB-based metal powder bed fusion cost and time estimator at amdsp.org.aalto.fi, splitting cost into machine amortisation, work and material; the 2020 report calls 2.0 'revised and expanded', adding polymer systems and cost and lead time over production volume.
description: Online calculator estimating AM part cost and lead time versus production volume and machine utilisation, using hexagonal close-packing nesting and support generation.
NRE_note: The 2.0 summary lists automatic orientation, support generation and nesting but does not say whether build preparation or design effort is costed, and the tool itself and any documenting paper could not be reached (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1).
Production_note: From an uploaded STL, the chosen machine, material and production volume, the tool computes part cost over volume with orientation, supports and nesting calculated, and the earlier version split cost into machine amortisation, work and material (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1; DIVA 2018 report, Sec. 3).
QA_Qual_note: The tool description names no qualification element, but it is a short summary rather than documentation, and the report's separate qualification case study is not tied to the calculator (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1, 5.2).
QA_Insp_note: Neither the 2.0 summary nor the earlier version's description (costs split into machine amortisation, work and material) names inspection cost, but both are short summaries and the tool could not be opened (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1; DIVA 2018 report, Sec. 3).
Storage_note: The earlier version accepted conventional piece, mould, storage and transport costs as comparison inputs, but the 2.0 summary does not mention storage and the tool could not be opened, so whether 2.0 keeps or uses these inputs is not shown (DIVA 2018 report, Sec. 3; VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1).
Shared_Capital_note: The tool outputs the cost associated with the machine's utilisation percentage and cost over production volume with hexagonal close-packing nesting of several parts per build, and the earlier version amortised the printer over eight years; sharing across users or sites is not modelled (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1; DIVA 2018 report, Sec. 3).
Shared_Capacity_note: One selected machine's capacity and utilisation are modelled and lead time grows with production volume, but no contention among different parts or users and no cross-site pooling is described (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1).
Speed_note: The tool reports 'the lead time over the production volume' as a computed output, not dollarised; how it is built up is not documented beyond build-process settings such as recoating times (VTT/Aalto 2020 report, Sec. 3.1).

name: DirectSpare spare part AM feasibility and cost decision support
year: Unknown start (36-month FP7 project); final report January 2012
developer: EU FP7 DirectSpare consortium (Materialise, Berenschot, BPO, Evonik, EOS, Fraunhofer ILT, Siemens, Eurocopter, BMW, Flying Cam, fcubic)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Management-level knock-out flowchart plus a six-area constraint model (engineering, material, process, economic, quality, ecological) and a questionnaire-based cost analysis tool for on-demand, on-location spare part production; a knowledge-based AM technology selector was planned.
NRE_note: The report discusses design effort for low-volume spares and offers a 'Copy Original Part' method (scan, unit-load FEA, geometry optimisation), but whether engineering effort enters the feasibility flowchart or cost tool cannot be confirmed from the publishable report (DirectSpare final report, sec. B.2).
Production_note: A questionnaire-based cost analysis tool built from influence parameters in an Ishikawa diagram is reported, but its inputs and formulas are not documented in the public report (DirectSpare final report, sec. B.5).
QA_Qual_note: Product quality is one of six knock-out constraint groups but its criteria are not described, and a certification process for AM spare parts is only called for, so whether qualification or certification gates the feasibility decision cannot be confirmed (DirectSpare final report, sec. B.1.2 and results section).
QA_Insp_note: Quality controls for order input data, the layering process and end parts are a separate quality-management objective and visual inspection appears in case examples, but inspection is not shown as a criterion of the knock-out flowchart or the cost tool (DirectSpare final report, sec. A, B.1.2 and B.3).
Storage_note: Cost reduction on stocks and warehousing and a 'balancing end of stock' business model are described as benefits, but stock does not appear as a criterion in the flowchart or constraint groups as reported (DirectSpare final report, executive summary, sec. B.1.2 and business models).
Shared_Capital_note: The public report mentions only investment in conventional tooling and moulds, not AM machine investment or its sharing, and the cost tool itself is not public, so the report cannot settle this (DirectSpare final report).
Shared_Capacity_note: A network of RTOs and industrial partners offering on-demand, on-location spare-part production is a project objective, not something the tools assign or route work across (DirectSpare final report, sec. A objective 16 and B.5).
Speed_note: The management-level knock-out flowchart includes manufacturing cost and time among its basic production-engineering checks, though how time is assessed is not described, while the delivery- and production-time scores are a sector-level market study and no lead time is computed (DirectSpare final report, sec. B.1.2 and B.1.3).

name: CASTOR (CASTOR Enterprise / automatic part identification)
year: 2020 (earliest coverage); Light/Enterprise/White Label editions by Jun 2021; 2D-drawing analysis Jul 2022; Oqton MOS integration Apr 2023; Siemens Xcelerator Nov 2023; used in NSRP Navy shipbuilding project May 2023-May 2024
developer: Castor Technologies Ltd. (described as Israeli in earlier coverage; Fabbaloo 2021 calls it California-based); resold by Siemens (CASTOR Enterprise; Teamcenter-X & CASTOR), integrated into Oqton MOS (Apr 2023), listed on Hexagon Nexus
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Bulk-screens 3D CAD, 2D PDF drawings, BOMs or part metadata spreadsheets. For each part it flags printability (printable / printable with changes / unprintable, with reasons such as threads, metal-support milling, heat deformation and wall thickness) and picks a printer and material. It then estimates AM cost and conventional-manufacturing cost in dollars, plus AM lead time in days. Other outputs: break-even versus CNC and die casting, redesign options (cheapest, best match, weight reduction, consolidation), FEA and CO2. Enterprise adds printer ROI calculations and a customizable calculation structure.
NRE_note: Classifies parts as 'printable with changes' with reasons such as threads and wall thickness and recommends design changes such as weight reduction, so redesign need enters its printability decision, but the engineering effort is not costed (NSRP deck 2024; 3D ADEPT interview).
Production_note: Outputs a per-part AM cost estimate in dollars on a named printer and material that changes with geometry and solution (check valve on SLM-280 in CuNi2SiCr $8,105.72 best match vs $3,989.52 weight-reduced; PA12 on Jet Fusion $368.98) beside a traditional-manufacturing estimate (NSRP deck 2024).
QA_Qual_note: The NSRP output tables have no qualification field and vendor pages mention only a comparison of printed-part mechanical properties with traditional materials, while the Enterprise calculation structure is customisable and not public, so qualification handling cannot be settled (NSRP deck 2024; Hexagon page; 3D ADEPT Enterprise launch).
QA_Insp_note: No source read, including the NSRP output tables and vendor pages, mentions inspection or testing (closest is a tolerance analysis), and the full cost model is not public (NSRP deck 2024; Hexagon page; 3D ADEPT interview).
Storage_note: CASTOR Enterprise lets users enter operational supply-chain costs 'such as inventory, shipment, labour costs' into its customisable cost estimate, an inventory cost element with no documented model of AM's effect on stock; Hexagon claims it identifies inventory cost savings (3D ADEPT Enterprise launch; Hexagon page).
Shared_Capital_note: CASTOR Enterprise outputs 'ROI calculations for 3D printers' and lets users set in-house printers for its analysis, but no amortisation, utilisation or volume inputs are documented (3D ADEPT interview; NSRP deck 2024).
Shared_Capacity_note: CASTOR says it connects manufacturers to its partner network of service bureaus as a 'traffic provider', but whether the software assigns or routes work among bureaus cannot be confirmed from public sources (3D ADEPT interview).
Speed_note: Outputs an AM lead-time estimate in days and an AM time-saving flag per part (check valve 19-23 days on Jet Fusion, 53-78 days on SLM-280), meeting the computed-lead-time test though no readiness value is attached (NSRP deck 2024).

name: 3YOURMIND Part Identification
year: Launch year not confirmed; sold as Part Screening & Business Case by Jan 2023, used in USMC screening from 2022, renamed Part Identification in 2024
developer: 3YOURMIND GmbH (Berlin); US federal work with Phillips Corp. Federal Division
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
earlier_versions: Additive Manufacturing Part Identifier (AMPI) (date not found): earlier name; 3YOURMIND's Jan 2025 FAQ says Part Identification was 'formerly known as' AMPI, and the 2025 review dates the renaming to 2024. | Part Screening & Business Case (Jan 2023): name used for the screening and business-case solution in 3YOURMIND's Jan 2023 FAQ, whose images are still labeled AMPI. | Agile PLM (date not found): given as an earlier name in the survey but not confirmed; the old 'Agile PLM FAQ' URL now serves Part Screening & Business Case content without mentioning Agile PLM.
description: Screens part inventories (3D CAD, 2D drawings via AI drawing analysis, or metadata only) for technical and economic AM suitability and recommends technologies. With optional economic inputs (current price, lead time, annual demand) it reports unit-cost comparison and savings broken into manufacturing cost, stock avoidance, downtime avoidance and lead-time reduction.
NRE_note: The tool gives DfAM optimisation suggestions and redesign recommendations 'when needed' and extracts data from 2D drawings, but it can assess parts from metadata alone and whether redesign need or CAD availability changes the suitability result cannot be confirmed from public sources (3YOURMIND software FAQ; product page).
Production_note: The Economics tab computes per-unit savings for each suggested technology broken into material, labour and overhead, against the entered original part price, using a customisable database of 800+ printers and 1,300+ materials (How to find 3D printable parts fast; 2D drawing analysis page; software FAQ).
QA_Qual_note: Screening gates parts on technical and financial feasibility before AM engineers test and qualify them and qualified parts are catalogued, but qualification is not named as a screening criterion, so whether the tool uses it to decide cannot be confirmed (3YOURMIND software FAQ; USMC case study).
QA_Insp_note: Product pages, FAQ, 2D-analysis page and the USMC case study do not mention inspection or testing cost, and no help documentation or model description is public (3YOURMIND pages).
Storage_note: With price, lead time and annual demand as inputs, the report overview outputs 'stock avoidance' as a savings component, and inventory scores can be set as KPIs (2D drawing analysis page; software FAQ).
Shared_Capital_note: Public pages name material, labour and overhead in per-unit economics but do not say whether machine depreciation or utilisation enters; the printer database can be customised with own machines and data (How to find 3D printable parts fast; software FAQ).
Shared_Capacity_note: Part Identification pages describe no capacity model; scheduling and utilisation suggestions belong to the separate MES product, and the full method is not public (software FAQ; 2D drawing analysis page).
Speed_note: Original lead time is an input and the report outputs lead-time reduction and 'downtime avoidance' savings within total savings (2D drawing analysis page; How to find 3D printable parts fast).

name: Senvol ML
developer: Senvol LLC (New York)
description: Machine-learning software linking process parameters, process signatures (in-situ monitoring) and material properties to optimize parameters, predict properties and generate statistically substantiated allowables with fewer test builds. It targets qualification cost rather than part screening or business cases.
NRE_note: The software optimises process parameters, predicts the parameters needed for target properties and recommends which data points to generate, claiming lower process-development time and cost, but parameter-development effort is an activity it performs, not a cost it uses to decide (Senvol ML product page).
Production_note: The documented scope is predictive models linking process parameters, process signatures and material properties for characterisation and qualification, which plainly excludes per-part production cost (Senvol ML product page).
QA_Qual_note: The software is said to tell the user how many builds and specimens to generate for a target confidence when qualifying AM machines and materials, which quantifies the material and process data-generation step only, with no part qualification, first-article or approval effort and no example output shown (Senvol ML product page; Navy STP spotlight 2021).
QA_Insp_note: Senvol ML uses process-signature data from in-situ monitoring as a model input to predict properties in support of quality assurance, but press sources show no inspection scope, step or cost entering a decision (Senvol ML product page; Digital Engineering 24/7 2021).
Storage_note: The documented scope is process-property machine learning for development and qualification, which plainly excludes spare-part inventory (Senvol ML product page).
Shared_Capital_note: The documented scope (process-property machine learning) plainly excludes machine investment, amortisation or utilisation (Senvol ML product page).
Shared_Capacity_note: The documented scope (process-property machine learning) plainly excludes print capacity shared across sites or users (Senvol ML product page).
Speed_note: The Navy STP spotlight claims that shortening material and part qualification speeds AM adoption and 'contributes to warfighter readiness', a claim in words, and the software's documented scope (process-property modelling and allowables for qualification) excludes part lead time or availability (Navy STP spotlight 2021).

name: Senvol Database
developer: Senvol LLC
description: Free searchable database of industrial AM machines and materials with 30+ search fields (e.g., build size, material type, tensile strength) for machine and material selection. No cost or part-screening functions documented.
NRE_note: The Senvol Database is a searchable machine and material specification database, a documented scope that plainly excludes design files, reverse engineering and parameter development (Senvol database page; 3DPI 2015).
Production_note: Machines and materials are searched by process, material type, build envelope, material properties and machine price, and no per-part production cost is computed (Senvol database page; 3dprint.com 2015).
QA_Qual_note: Materials can be searched by certifications and tests (e.g. flammability, USP Class VI, both polymer-oriented examples), so certification status is a screening filter, but no qualification effort or cost is set out (3dprint.com 2015).
QA_Insp_note: As a machine and material specification database, per-part inspection and testing are outside its documented scope (Senvol database page).
Storage_note: The database holds machine and material records only, so parts inventory is outside its documented scope (Senvol database page).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine price is a searchable machine field, so purchase cost serves as a screening filter, but nothing spreads that capital across parts or users (3dprint.com 2015).
Shared_Capacity_note: The database holds machine and material records only and has no capacity or network function (Senvol database page).
Speed_note: As a specification database searched by make, model, process, material, build envelope and price, it estimates neither build time nor lead time (Senvol database page; 3dprint.com 2015).

name: 3D Spark (Part Screening, Make-or-Buy Support, quoting)
year: Founding year not confirmed; in commercial use by 2022 (Alstom savings) and deployed at Deutsche Bahn in Oct 2023
developer: 3D Spark GmbH (Hamburg; Fraunhofer IAPT spin-off)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Screens part portfolios from CAD, drawings and/or ERP exports, calculating cost per part, lead time and CO2 for AM and conventional routes, in-house and at suppliers, with technical/economic suitability ratings and break-even curves. Process chains include pre-processing, build time and post-processing, calibrated to the customer's equipment (reported +/-5% at DB).
NRE_note: Preparation steps are costed per part, job or lot in the process chain (e.g. a standard preparation time), but redesign is offered only as optional AMPOWER partner consulting and no one-time design or parameter cost is documented (3D Spark KB: manually updating process steps; part screening page).
Production_note: Cost per part, job or lot is computed per technology from material cost per kg, machine hourly rate and build rates, labour and machine time, and pre/post-process steps with cost drivers, calibrated to the customer's equipment (3D Spark KB: machine and material properties, process-chain spreadsheet; Metal AM on DB).
QA_Qual_note: Product pages and the support knowledge base do not mention part, material or process qualification, and the cost-settings content is not public (3D Spark part screening and make-or-buy pages; KB global settings).
QA_Insp_note: Users can add their own pre/post-process steps with a cost driver (EUR/h, /job, /part), but no documentation names an inspection or testing step, so whether inspection is costed is not shown (3D Spark KB: process-chain spreadsheet, process steps).
Storage_note: The platform analyses part portfolios from ERP data and keeps screened parts in a digital warehouse, but no stock level or holding cost is used in screening or make-or-buy decisions (3D Spark part screening pages; make-or-buy FAQ).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine time cost is shared across parts in a nested build ('Shared Build Jobs' with a nesting-density input that distributes production expenses across components) and cost per part is charted against lot size, a multi-part-build assumption; the 21.1% utilisation figure in a vendor case is not documented as tool output (3D Spark KB: mixed nesting, break-even chart; 441-parts blog).
Shared_Capacity_note: The make-or-buy module recommends per part whether to keep work on in-house machines or outsource it to the supplier network ('Keep your machines for the right jobs and outsource the rest'), but no capacity, utilisation or pooling calculation is documented and capacity does not feed lead time (3D Spark make-or-buy page; KB).
Speed_note: The software calculates process time and lead time for each step of each production option (technology, in-house or supplier) alongside cost and CO2, and lead time can be manually overridden (3D Spark KB: manually updating process steps; part screening page).

name: PrintSyst.ai 3DP AI-Perfecter
developer: PrintSyst.ai (Israel, founded 2017)
description: AI-based automatic pre-printing part analysis that gives printing recommendations and a dashboard, aimed at replacing manual engineering review before printing. No documented cost, lead-time or inventory outputs.
