NRE_note: The report lists machine setup among ill-structured costs and names design cost as the exception to cost-free customisation, but its own C_AM decomposition has no engineering or setup term and the setup figures it reports are Hopkinson and Dickens', Lindemann's and Atzeni and Salmi's (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3, 3.3, 4.3, Table 3.1).
Production_note: The report's own total-cost decomposition (C_AM) carries AM manufacturing cost only as a lumped process term (P_M,AM, said to include administrative and machine costs) with no build-up from machine time or material; the per-part build-ups it presents are Hopkinson and Dickens' and Ruffo et al.'s models, which it summarises (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 4.1, 4.3).
QA_Qual_note: The full report was read; qualification and certification are not treated as cost items, and quality and standards appear only as general adoption needs (NIST SP 1176).
QA_Insp_note: Quality assurance is discussed as a concern needing standard methods to evaluate accuracy, surface finish and feature detail, and build failure is listed as an ill-structured cost, but neither enters the report's cost equations (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3, 3.3).
Storage_note: The report's own decomposition includes material and finished-goods inventory terms and it estimates a macro holding cost ($52 billion at an assumed 25% of $208 billion inventory), but AM's effect on stock is not modelled (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3.1.1, 4.3).
Shared_Capital_note: The report says only that exhausting the build space is a significant efficiency factor and that fully utilising the build chamber cuts per-unit cost, and its own C_AM equation has no capital, amortisation or utilisation term; the depreciation and utilisation figures are Hopkinson and Dickens' and Ruffo et al.'s assumptions (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3.2.3, 4.1, 4.3, 6).
Shared_Capacity_note: Centralised vs distributed production is discussed by quoting Khajavi et al.'s F-18 spare-parts case ($1.0M vs $1.8M per year) and decentralisation's effect on disruption, which the report reviews rather than computes (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3.1.2, 3.1.4).
Speed_note: Time appears only as a conceptual term in the total-advantage equations (TA_T), which the authors say cannot yet be measured, and in narrative on on-demand parts and supply disruption, so time changes no output of the report's method (NIST SP 1176, Secs. 3.1.2, 3.1.4, 4.4).

name: Ghadge aircraft spare parts AM system dynamics model
developer: Abhijeet Ghadge, Georgia Karantoni, Atanu Chaudhuri, Aravindan Srinivasan (Heriot-Watt University; Aalborg University)
description: System dynamics simulation comparing CM base-stock inventory across RDCs and service locations with on-demand AM at service locations; AM inventory ~25% of CM and 5-year holding cost ~$1M vs >$4.5M.
NRE_note: The full text and Vensim equations contain no design, digitisation or engineering cost variable; the only cost variable is holding cost per unit (author version, Appendices 1-2).
Production_note: Production cost is not a model variable; the authors only expect in words a moderate rise in raw-material and 3D-production unit cost, which the model does not use (author version, Sec. 5.1, Appendix 2).
QA_Qual_note: The full text has no qualification variable or treatment of AM qualification: quality standards appear only in the literature review and literature-based limitations table, and certification only as a rationale for the conventional network's regional centres (author version, Sec. 2.1, Table 1, Sec. 4.1.1, Appendices 1-2).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection and testing are absent from the text, model equations and parameter tables (author version, Appendices 1-2).
Storage_note: Aggregate inventory and accumulated holding cost ($15/unit) are computed for both networks, with AM inventory about 25% of CM and 5-year holding cost just over $1M vs over $4.5M (author version, Sec. 4.3.1-4.3.2).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine acquisition cost is not a model input, and high investment cost is named only in the literature table and limitations, with nothing on amortisation or sharing (author version, Table 1, Sec. 5.2).
Shared_Capacity_note: One aggregate AM machine-capacity stock (105,000 units) is drawn down by production across all service locations, but it never binds and has no effect on lead time or service, and there is no per-site pooling (author version, Appendix 2).
Speed_note: Stochastic replenishment and AM production lead times delay order fulfilment and set safety stock, but backorders are computed only in the CM model, so AM's availability effect is not reported or valued (author version, Appendix 2).

name: Sgarbossa conventional vs additive spare parts inventory comparison (Poisson demand)
developer: Fabio Sgarbossa, Mirco Peron (NTNU); Francesco Lolli, Elia Balugani (University of Modena and Reggio Emilia)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Periodic-review Poisson inventory model choosing manufacturing option, review period and order-up-to level, with technology-specific unit costs (from experts) and AM-vs-CM failure-rate ratios from fatigue literature; decision trees show backorder cost (~EUR 3,500/unit split) is the main driver and that AM wins whenever storage is zero.
NRE_note: Design and redesign costs are explicitly left to future work and the objective Ctot = Ch + Cb + Cp has no NRE term (accepted manuscript, Eq. 3, Conclusions).
Production_note: Unit production cost per option is computed from expert EUR/cm3 rates by technology (SLM, LENS, casting, wrought, forging) and post-process EUR/h for polishing, annealing and HIP by part size band (accepted manuscript, Tables 4-6).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification and certification are not modelled; reliability enters only through literature-based AM vs CM MTTF ratios (accepted manuscript, Eqs. 1-2, Table 3).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection and testing costs are absent; only post-processing (polishing, annealing, HIP) is in unit cost (accepted manuscript, Tables 4-6).
Storage_note: Holding cost (30% per year of unit cost) is computed on average stock under the optimal order-up-to level, with storage limits Smax = 0 and 1 tested (accepted manuscript, Eqs. 3-6).
Shared_Capital_note: AM machine capital is absent (unit cost is the only AM cost input) and limited AM equipment capacity is named as future work (accepted manuscript, Conclusions).
Shared_Capacity_note: It is a single-item, single-stock-point model and limited AM equipment capacity and multi-item settings are left to future work (accepted manuscript, Conclusions).
Speed_note: Expected backorders over review period plus lead time are computed and costed (1,000-51,000 EUR/unit), with CM lead times of 4-12 weeks and AM lead time equal to total production time (accepted manuscript, Eqs. 3-5, Table 6).

name: Peron failure-rate-uncertainty AM vs CM spare parts model with inspection tools
developer: Mirco Peron, Andrea M. Coruzzolo, Rob Basten, Nils Knofius, Francesco Lolli, Fabio Sgarbossa
description: Periodic-review Poisson inventory model with materials-science-based failure-rate uncertainty showing AM is penalized far more than CM by uncertainty; porosity assessment or in-situ monitoring pays off only if it cuts uncertainty by ~5-6 percentage points.
NRE_note: The 2024 abstract does not mention design or one-time cost and the precursor has only holding, backorder and production terms, but the 2024 full text could not be fetched (proxy refused the repository PDF), so whether the extension adds NRE is not shown (UNIMORE abstract; IFAC 2022, Eq. 1).
Production_note: The 2024 abstract names AM's high production costs as the side traded against inventory savings, and the precursor of the same model enters per-technology unit production costs (CM EUR 30, AM EUR 150) as inputs to the production cost term (UNIMORE abstract; IFAC 2022, Eq. 4, Table 1).
QA_Qual_note: Neither the 2024 abstract nor the precursor mentions qualification or certification; failure-rate uncertainty is derived from fatigue-curve spread and attributed to AM's newness, and the 2024 full text could not be read (UNIMORE abstract; IFAC 2022 full text).
QA_Insp_note: The model weighs investing in porosity assessment or in-situ monitoring and computes the uncertainty reduction each needs to pay off (about 5 and 6 percentage points), but the abstract does not show whether inspection is costed per part or per build or as a lump investment (UNIMORE abstract; IDEAS record).
Storage_note: A periodic-review Poisson inventory model sets order-up-to levels for AM and CM, and the precursor computes holding cost (0.58% of unit cost per week) on expected stock on hand, quantifying AM's inventory reduction (UNIMORE abstract; IFAC 2022, Eq. 2).
Shared_Capital_note: Neither the 2024 abstract nor the precursor includes AM machine capital (unit cost is a single input), but the 2024 full text could not be fetched to confirm the extension adds none (IFAC 2022 full text; UNIMORE abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: The model is a single-item periodic-review inventory model with fixed lead times (0.1 weeks AM, 4 weeks CM in the precursor), so shared printer capacity is outside its documented scope (UNIMORE abstract; IFAC 2022, Table 1).
Speed_note: The precursor of the same periodic-review Poisson model computes and costs expected backorders over review period plus lead time with AM and CM lead times of 0.1 and 4 weeks, and the 2024 abstract credits AM's quick supply for its advantage; the 2024 backorder formulation itself was not read (IFAC 2022, Eq. 3, Table 1; UNIMORE abstract).

name: Ahlsell automotive slow-moving spare parts AM supply chain cost model
developer: Levin Ahlsell, Didar Jalal, Patrik Jonsson (Chalmers); Siavash H. Khajavi, Jan Holmstrom (Aalto)
description: Total supply chain cost model (production price, inbound/outbound transport, ABC-based warehousing, and service costs incl. vehicle-off-road downtime, badwill, lost sales) over the part life cycle; 3 of 14 parts show savings; metal AM parts cost ~1,756% more and need 72-99% cost cuts to break even.
NRE_note: The full text states the model does not include the cost of developing a missing 3D drawing and leaves redesign engineering labour uncosted, so there is no one-time engineering term (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.1, Discussion).
Production_note: Part-specific unit prices for each technology are explicit model inputs, AM from supplier quotes on 3D drawings and TM from the OEM database, which meets the per-technology unit-cost input test (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.1, Appendix A).
QA_Qual_note: The full text explicitly excludes the cost of quality controls to approve a spare part and has no qualification term (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.1).
QA_Insp_note: Quality-control cost is explicitly excluded and quality-check time is also left out of the AM lead time (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.1, 4.1.6).
Storage_note: ABC-based warehousing cost, including capital cost on stock value, is computed from average inventory that differs by method (TM lifetime buy vs AM replenishment with a one-piece safety stock), so AM's effect on stock is quantified (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.3-4.1.4, Table 4).
Shared_Capital_note: AM is outsourced and machine capital sits inside the supplier price with its margin, so the documented scope has no capital, utilisation or sharing term (Chalmers full text, Sec. 3.4, Discussion).
Shared_Capacity_note: One outsourced centralised supplier is modelled with no capacity constraint, and the authors state a dispersed AM supply chain was not investigated (Chalmers full text, Sec. 3.4, Discussion).
Speed_note: Service loss is costed as vehicle-off-road fees, badwill and lost sales, with the AM stockout penalty set by the AM supplier lead time; the AM service level itself is an assumed constant (Chalmers full text, Sec. 4.1.4, 4.1.6).

name: Strong two-stage p-median model for metal AM post-processing hubs
developer: Danielle Strong, Michael Kay, Brett Conner, Thomas Wakefield, Guha Manogharan (Penn State and collaborators)
description: Two-stage p-median facility location model choosing hub locations and capacities and assigning demand across machine shops and heat-treatment facilities, minimizing fixed, operating and transport costs; 22 hubs grow to 35 as demand rises.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was reachable; it bases the model on geography, demand and fixed and operational costs and does not mention design or engineering cost (Penn State Pure abstract).
Production_note: Operational costs of hybrid-AM processing at hubs enter the p-median objective at hub level, with no per-part build-up (Penn State Pure abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract was reachable and it does not mention qualification (Penn State Pure abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract was reachable; it covers heat treatment and machining but does not say whether inspection is in the operational costs (Penn State Pure abstract).
Storage_note: Only the abstract was reachable and it does not mention inventory (Penn State Pure abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The two-stage p-median model chooses hub locations and capacities by trading fixed hub costs against operational and transport costs, with 22 hubs growing to 35 as demand rises (Penn State Pure abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: Hub capacities, capacity utilisation and demand assignment across machine shops, heat-treatment facilities and hubs are outputs, but no effect on lead time or service is shown (Penn State Pure abstract).
Speed_note: Only the abstract was reachable; it reports transport cost but not lead or delivery time (Penn State Pure abstract).

name: Barz two-stage capacitated facility location model with AM buy-to-fly ratio
developer: Andreas Barz, Tobias Buer, Hans-Dietrich Haasis
description: Two-stage capacitated facility location problem showing that lower buy-to-fly ratios (AM) cut transport costs and shift production sites closer to customers, with the site count roughly unchanged.
NRE_note: The objective contains only transport costs and site-opening fixed costs, so no design or engineering effort is modelled (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Eq. 1).
Production_note: Production costs are explicitly left out of the experiments because they are treated as independent of the site (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 4.2.3).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is absent from the full paper, whose only AM input is the buy-to-fly ratio in the flow-balance constraint (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 3.3.2).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection is absent from the full paper; the objective and constraints cost only transport and site opening (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Eq. 1-8).
Storage_note: Storage of raw materials or products at production sites is explicitly forbidden, so inventory is outside the model (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 3.1-3.2).
Shared_Capital_note: Fixed costs of opening capacitated sites are traded against transport cost, but these are generic site costs rather than AM machine capital and scale economies are explicitly not modelled (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 3.2, 4.2.3).
Shared_Capacity_note: Site capacities of 100-500 units constrain the assignment of customers to sites, but there is no lead-time, delivery-time or service-level effect (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 3.3.3).
Speed_note: The model has no time variable and lists slower AM production time only as future work (Barz et al. 2016 full text, Sect. 5).

name: Doudnikoff NCSU/USMA military spare parts network model (extends McDermott et al.)
developer: Letai M. Doudnikoff (advisor Brandon M. McConnell), North Carolina State University
earlier_versions: McDermott, Winz, Hodgson, Kay, King & McConnell 2021 (Journal of Defense Analytics and Logistics 5(2):179; from McDermott's 2020 NCSU MS thesis, with the Winz et al. 2020 readiness-vs-cost working paper): the original Monte Carlo + Croston/SBA intermittent-demand + MILP (s,S) model comparing no-AM, centralized and distributed AM. It found centralized AM wins for lumpy demand and distributed for stable demand. Doudnikoff 2021 reuses this model and its 1-1-4 network and modifies it for isolated military sustainment networks, first-machine placement and AM fixed-cost/capacity trade-offs.
description: MILP inventory policy plus Monte Carlo simulation (60 periods) for first-machine placement and isolated-network studies; distributed first machine lowers operating and transport cost, but no-AM is cheapest once AM fixed cost is included; returns to added AM capacity diminish.
NRE_note: The MILP objective covers TM and AM production, transport, carrying and backorder costs only and parts are unspecified, so no design or engineering cost appears (NCSU thesis, Eq. 3.2, Assumption 2).
Production_note: AM per-part production cost is a model term but is set equal to TM cost for simplicity, a lumped unit cost with no build-up from machine time or material (NCSU thesis, Assumption 4, Eq. 3.2).
QA_Qual_note: The model assumes equal AM and TM build quality, which places qualification outside its documented scope (NCSU thesis, Assumption 3).
QA_Insp_note: No inspection or testing term appears in the cost objective and build quality is assumed equal to TM (NCSU thesis, Eq. 3.2, Assumption 3).
Storage_note: The MILP outputs order-up-to levels for an (s,S) policy per product, DC and AM configuration and charges inventory carrying cost at DCs and service locations (NCSU thesis, Sec. 3.4.2, 3.4.7, Table 3.1).
Shared_Capital_note: AM fixed cost ($121/$241/$512 per machine per day) is charged by the number of machines in the network, and centralized vs distributed placement and added capacity are traded off with fixed-cost sensitivity (NCSU thesis, Sec. 3.4.6.1, Table 3.1).
Shared_Capacity_note: AM output per node and period is capped by capacity (one product type per period) and a centralized AM machine at the DC serves all service locations, so capacity contention drives backorders, a model measure; one shared site, no cross-site pooling beyond the DC (NCSU thesis, Eqs. 3.15-3.16, Sec. 4.2).
Speed_note: Transport lead times set reorder points from lead-time demand, and total backorders and backorder penalty cost are model measures (NCSU thesis, Eq. 3.1, Sec. 4.2, Table 3.1).

name: Coyle naval aviation AM sustainment screening + DES (NPS)
developer: David M. Coyle (Naval Postgraduate School)
description: Top-down screen of Navy aviation inventory for AM candidates followed by an Innoslate discrete-event simulation (adapted from Jedeck 2015) comparing local stock, OEM order and local AM for one part: AM $3,145 in ~10 days vs OEM $7,005 in 545 days; at quarter print speed AM costs 17% more but stays far faster.
NRE_note: Per-build machine setup is costed ($100, 1 h), but the model assumes a CAD file, PMI and TDP exist and omits reverse-engineering cost and time, citing SD-22's three to six months only in discussion (full thesis, Table 4, Sec. V.B.1).
Production_note: Per-part local AM cost is built from setup, machine run ($550.10 for an 18.6 h build from build rate and part volume), removal, post-processing and feedstock at $47.62/lb as triangular distributions, with print-speed sensitivity (full thesis, Tables 3-4, Sec. V.B.3, V.D).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is discussed as depending on item criticality, but its times are explicitly excluded from the simulation and left for future work, so it does not enter the screen or the model (full thesis, Sec. VI.A).
QA_Insp_note: Final inspection is a per-part activity in the AM branch at $400 and 1 day (full thesis, Table 4).
Storage_note: A holding cost rate is computed for the local-stock branch (h = 10% x $7,004.77 = $700.48 per unit-year), but stock levels are not modelled (the branch only decrements one unit), no stock-branch total is reported and results compare only AM and OEM unit prices (full thesis, Sec. V.B.3.a, V.C).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine time is priced as one run cost ($550.10 for 18.6 h, from Ray 2017 ABC models) with one part per run and no depreciation, utilisation or multi-part input (full thesis, Table 4, Sec. V.B).
Shared_Capacity_note: The DES models one part on one EOS M290 at one FRC with no capacity constraint, print queue, competing parts or multiple sites, and the conclusions do not raise capacity sharing; networks appear only in the literature review and a remark that FRCs could host AM (full thesis, Sec. II.C.2, III.B, V.B, VI).
Speed_note: The DES outputs time per activity for each supply branch, giving AM lead time of about 10 days vs 545 days for an OEM order, with print-speed sensitivity (full thesis, Sec. V.C-V.D).

name: Busachi/Erkoyuncu (Cranfield, Babcock) AM framework and decision support for Royal Navy support services
developer: Alessandro Busachi, John Erkoyuncu, Paul Colegrove (Cranfield University); Richard Drake, Chris Watts, Stephen Wilding (Babcock International)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Soft-systems framework with eight phases (mission, platform, configuration, critical-to-availability parts, AM technology, DfAM, manufacturing configuration, dynamic simulation) and availability equations in which on-platform AM removes administrative and procurement delay; authors state benefits still need quantification.
NRE_note: Design time (DesTim) is a default input reported as a meta output and the companion FDM model costs bidding and geometry preparation 'at a high level', but no WAAM cost equation (Eqs. 4-15) contains a design term and WAAM geometry-preparation costs were 'modelled but not included', so there is no one-time redesign or reverse-engineering cost term (Busachi PhD thesis Table 10, Secs. 5.3, 7.2; Procedia CIRP 67, 2018, Sec. 6).
Production_note: Per-part WAAM cost is computed from material (deposited, substrate, waste), deposition (utilities, wire change, machine hourly rate), setup and unloading using machine, engineer and machining rates, e.g. GBP 75,732 for case component 1 (Busachi PhD thesis, Sec. 5.3, Eqs. 4-15, Sec. 8.2.1).
QA_Qual_note: Phase 7 (manufacturing configuration) lists 'perform a qualification of the component' as an activity and the discussion names qualification the main constraint, but qualification is not a gate and no qualification cost or time enters the availability equations or any decision (IJSAEM 2018, Secs. 7.2, 9; PhD thesis Secs. 6.2, 8.1).
QA_Insp_note: '3D Scanner (QA)' is a cost element in the FDM cost breakdown and the scanner, used 'for Quality Assurance to measure the physical tolerances of the part', has its own machine rate from investment, utilisation and overheads (Eq. 1), but scanner time per part is not modelled ('should be modelled as these might consume time') and no inspection value is given (Procedia CIRP 67, 2018, Secs. 6.1, 7, 8; Busachi PhD thesis Fig. 41, Sec. 5.4).
Storage_note: Lower platform inventory and freed space are claimed, with warehouses shifting to digital files plus powder and wire stocks, but inventory does not enter the availability equations or any decision (IJSAEM 2018, Secs. 9-10; PhD thesis Sec. 8.3).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine and WAAM system rates are computed from investment, time of utilisation and utilisation rate with overheads (Eq. 6; Table 10 inputs Inv, TimUti, RatUti), and setup cost is divided by batch size (Eq. 14) (Busachi PhD thesis, Secs. 5.2, 5.3).
Shared_Capacity_note: Machine utilisation is a model input and AM location configurations (in-port, support vessel, forward base, on-platform) are modelled through distance-based travel time, but AM utilisation is assumed 'limitless', so platforms never contend for capacity (PhD thesis Secs. 5.2, 7.3, Eq. 16; IJSAEM 2018, Sec. 8).
Speed_note: The DSS computes travel time, logistic delay time, downtime and operational availability (Eqs. 16-22), e.g. availability rising from 96.47% to 99.25% as LDT falls from about 661 h to 6.7 h (Busachi PhD thesis, Secs. 5.3.3, 8.2.2, Table 18).

name: Strieby USMC expeditionary metal AM cost-effectiveness analysis
developer: LtCol Stephen F. Strieby, USMC (Naval Postgraduate School, Acquisition Research Program)
description: Cost-effectiveness ratio (total system cost / parts produced over a 5-year life, from representative print times) for four metal AM processes with sensitivity on print and sintering times; recommends hybrid wire-arc AM.
NRE_note: Design time per unique part and the MCO 4700.4 design, test-fit and approval process are described, but design effort is left out of the CEA as equal across alternatives, so it does not affect the ranking (NPS report NPS-LM-23-263, ch. V).
Production_note: Cost per part is purchase price divided by lifetime operating hours times a representative production time per technology; material, labour and maintenance are excluded, so only a machine-time term is built up (NPS report, ch. V).
QA_Qual_note: The CEA assumes qualification will be resolved and costs nothing; the MCO 4700.4 approval process is discussed and a standardised test print is recommended, neither used in the analysis (NPS report, ch. V-VI).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection, NDT and part testing are not discussed or costed in the full report; 'test and evaluation' refers to acquisition of the systems and is treated as equal across them (NPS report, full text).
Storage_note: The report frames AM as shrinking stockpiles of repair and replacement parts, but the CEA uses only printer cost per part produced and explicitly ignores raw-material inventory, so stock does not enter the analysis (NPS report NPS-LM-23-263, abstract, ch. II and ch. V Step 5).
Shared_Capital_note: Each system's purchase price is amortised over 15,600 lifetime operating hours (12 h/day, 5 days/week, 5 years) and the parts produced in that time, a utilisation and volume assumption, with sensitivity on lifetime operating hours (NPS report, ch. V, Table 25).
Shared_Capacity_note: The CEA assumes an in-theatre printer can be tasked by any task-force organisation under a prioritisation process, but the analysis does not assign or route work and models no queue; a queuing study of XFAB numbers is left to future work (NPS report, ch. V-VI).
Speed_note: Representative production time per process (e.g. 9 h hybrid, 6 h ElemX, 61.5 h FFF/BMD) sets parts produced and drives the sensitivity analysis, but lead time and readiness are explicitly not computed (NPS report, ch. V).

name: NASA-STD-6030 Additive Manufacturing Requirements for Spaceflight Systems (2021)
developer: NASA (Marshall Space Flight Center; NASA Engineering and Safety Center)
earlier_versions: MSFC-STD-3716 (2017): Marshall standard for L-PBF spaceflight hardware; superseded by NASA-STD-6030 in 2021, which extended it to other AM processes. | MSFC-SPEC-3717 (2017): Marshall specification for control and qualification of L-PBF metallurgical processes; superseded in 2021 by NASA-STD-6030 and companion NASA-SPEC-6033.
description: Classifies each AM part by consequence of failure (Class A/B/C, plus Exempt), then structural demand and a points-based AM risk score (inspectability, removable as-built surfaces, supports, wall thickness) into subclasses A1–A4/B1–B4, and tailors the QA requirements (QMP, material property suite, witness testing, NDE, preproduction articles, part process qualification) to each class.
NRE_note: One-time engineering deliverables are mandatory but not costed: a QMP qualified per machine before production use, a Part Production Plan needing NASA approval, and a Qualified Part Process frozen after the AM Readiness Review (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 1.4, 3.2, AMR-47).
Production_note: Standard text read: no per-part production cost; cost appears only in the remark that Class C requirements 'were simplified to reduce cost, schedule, and complexity' (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 4.3.1.3).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is prescribed by class in countable form: QMP-A/B/C scaled to part class, a lot-mature property suite of at least 5 feedstock lots and 10 build cycles, six tensile coupons to qualify a Class C process, and a preproduction article evaluation for Class A/B parts (removed for C) (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 1.4, 3.2, 4.3.1.3, AMR-31, AMR-47).
QA_Insp_note: Per-build witness specimens are set by subclass (metals, independent builds: 6 tensile for A1-B4 and 2 for C, plus HCF, microstructure and chemistry by subclass; continuous builds: 4 tensile), and full surface and volume NDE is required for Class A and B parts, removed for C (NASA-STD-6030, Tables 5 and 7, AMR-17, AMR-19).
Storage_note: Inventory is not addressed; serialisation exists only for traceability to the build cycle, feedstock lots and records (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 4.12, AMR-26).
Shared_Capital_note: One-time qualification is reused across parts without numbers: a QMP tied to a machine serial number covers parts of equal or lower class (QMP-A for A, B and C), and a Sub-QMP on an equivalent machine inherits a parent QMP with reduced testing (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 3.2, 5, AMR-48).
Shared_Capacity_note: Capacity shared across sites or users is not addressed; machines enter only as the unit to which a QMP is registered (NASA-STD-6030 text).
Speed_note: Part lead time or availability is not addressed; schedule appears only as programmatic risk when witness testing lags part processing (NASA-STD-6030, Sec. 4.11).

name: USAF Structures Bulletin EZ-SB-19-01: Durability and Damage Tolerance Certification for AM Aircraft Structural Metallic Parts
developer: U.S. Air Force, AFLCMC/EZ (Engineering Directorate)
description: Sets durability and damage-tolerance certification requirements for metal AM structural parts by ASIP category (Fracture Critical Traceable/Non-Traceable, Durability Critical, Normal Controls), using equivalent initial damage size at category-specific exceedance probabilities and validated NDI capability. It recommends gaining experience in order of escalating criticality (NC, then DC, then FC).
NRE_note: Requires material and process selections to be evaluated for maturity and the AM equipment to be shown in control through manufacturing instructions, with machine qualification, software version control and periodic requalification, as conditions of certification, but none of this effort is costed (EZ-SB-19-01, Discussion, secs. 3.2, 4).
Production_note: Cost enters only through the required Stability and Producibility evaluations, whether 'predictable costs can be achieved' and whether scale-up proceeds 'without adversely affecting performance, costs, and quality', which must be satisfied before parts selection, with no per-part cost (EZ-SB-19-01, Discussion, factors 1-2; sec. 4).
QA_Qual_note: Sets class-specific analysis criteria (EIDS exceedance 1e-1 for NC, 1e-3 for DC and FC, 1e-7 for FC damage tolerance), but specimen counts and test frequencies are 'as approved by the procuring agency', so the campaign cannot be costed by class (EZ-SB-19-01, secs. 2.2, 3.3, 4).
QA_Insp_note: Requires NDI with a 95%-confidence POD for structural parts, production-part coupons, dissection or validated in-process monitoring and dimensional checks, with frequencies left to the procuring agency and no split by NC/DC/FC (EZ-SB-19-01, secs. 3.3-3.5).
Storage_note: Full bulletin read: spares, inventory and replacement-part stock are not mentioned (EZ-SB-19-01).
Shared_Capital_note: The bulletin allows test results from other efforts under the same sec. 3 controls to be used or combined, and specimen EIDS data to stand in until part data exist, so qualification data pooled across parts and machines feeds certification, with no numbers (EZ-SB-19-01, secs. 4, 4.1).
Shared_Capacity_note: Full bulletin read: machines appear only for traceability and EIDS variation across machines, never as shared print capacity (EZ-SB-19-01, secs. 3.7, 4.1).
Speed_note: Full bulletin read: the only timing language is that inspection and repair methods be available or developed 'in a timely manner', and part lead time or availability is not addressed (EZ-SB-19-01, Discussion, sec. 3.4).

name: USAF Flight Systems Bulletin EN-FSB-25-01 (Preliminary Qualification Data Requirements for Metallic AM) and Part Family Qualification approach
year: Unknown (bulletin number suggests 2025; the public abstract gives no date)
developer: U.S. Air Force (approach presented by M. Benedict at TMS 2026; issuing office not stated in the public abstract)
description: Separates material qualification from part certification and defines a standard minimum data set for screening new AM processes, materials and vendors on stability, producibility and predictability. It replaces 'point qualification' of each part with 'Part Family Qualification'.
NRE_note: Only a conference abstract describes the bulletin, whose scope is preliminary data to screen new processes, materials and vendors; whether it requires or addresses process-parameter development cannot be established, and the citing RFI asks only for documentation of process controls (TMS 2026 abstract; Govly RFI).
Production_note: A qualification-data bulletin for screening processes, materials and vendors; per-part production cost is plainly outside its documented scope (TMS 2026 abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Defines a standard minimum data set to judge material stability, producibility and predictability and whether further qualification investment is worthwhile, but its test counts, any class tiers and costs are not public (TMS 2026 abstract).
QA_Insp_note: The abstract does not list the data set's contents and the citing RFI asks for mechanical data and build-quality evidence without naming NDI or CT, so per-part inspection cannot be established (TMS 2026 abstract; Govly RFI).
Storage_note: Spare-part shortages appear only as motivation; inventory is plainly outside the documented scope of a qualification-data bulletin (TMS 2026 abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The approach replaces point qualification, which requalifies a part after every process or machine change, with Part Family Qualification that qualifies once for a family of parts, described without numbers (TMS 2026 abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: Print capacity and its pooling are plainly outside the documented scope of a qualification-data bulletin (TMS 2026 abstract).
Speed_note: Claims AM can overcome lead times that can take years and that Part Family Qualification cuts qualification time; whether the approach uses lead time in any decision cannot be confirmed from the abstract (TMS 2026 abstract).

name: NAVSEA AM qualification framework: Guidance letter Ser 05T/2018-024 severity levels, T9074-AX-GIB-010/100 material selection requirements, and PBF/DED Technical Publications
year: 2018 (guidance letter); 2020 (PBF Tech Pub); 2021 (DED Tech Pub, anticipated)
developer: Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA 05T, AM Technical Warrant Holder); DED tech pub developed with NSWC Carderock and EWI
description: Part failure-consequence severity (NAVSEA 5100.12-M Levels 1–7/N/A) determines whether material selection requirements and process/material qualification apply, whether a Technical Data Package is needed, and who approves. The process Tech Pubs then prescribe procedure qualification, part verification builds and a production conformance test plan.
NRE_note: One-time engineering deliverables are required by severity without cost: TDP fabrication requirements per Enclosure 5 for all but Level 7/N/A, NAVSEA-approved calibration plans, and an approved DED Procedure before procedure qualification (Ser 05T/2018-024 para 10, Encl. 3; Hovanec 2021).
Production_note: Cost appears only as the claim that AM enables 'cost-effective, on-demand manufacturing of critical parts'; per-part costing is outside the framework, with NAVSUP's separate cost/part tool handled apart from it (Ser 05T/2018-024 para 3; Rettaliata 2020).
QA_Qual_note: Severity Levels 1-5 switch on T9074-AX-GIB-010/100 and process/material qualification and the risk level sets the approval authority, but test content is left to the design activity part by part ('shall develop testing and qualification requirements (shock, NDE, etc.)'); the only countable items are one procedure-qualification build with PQTR per process/material combination and one sacrificial part-verification build with witness coupons, with no test counts by class (Ser 05T/2018-024, Encl. 2 paras 4b, 7, 9; Hovanec 2021).
QA_Insp_note: Per-build conformance testing and first-article test plans are required, and NDE types are set by material group with MIL-STD-2035 Class 1 acceptance, though schedules are set part by part in each Production Conformance Evaluation Plan rather than by severity class (Ser 05T/2018-024 para 3, Encl. 4; Hovanec 2021).
Storage_note: The guidance letter, read in full, does not address inventory or stock; 'on-demand manufacturing' appears once as a general benefit, not as an inventory element (Ser 05T/2018-024).
Shared_Capital_note: Qualification reuse is a rule of the procedure: procedure qualification 'is only intended to be done once for a combination of deposition process and material' and then applies 'irrespective of part geometry', with no numbers on the saving (Hovanec 2021).
Shared_Capacity_note: Neither the guidance letter (read in full) nor the Tech Pub briefing addresses capacity shared across ships, depots or users (Ser 05T/2018-024; Hovanec 2021).
Speed_note: Speed appears only as the claim that AM 'can shorten the design-to-production cycle', and lead time enters no step of the framework (Ser 05T/2018-024 para 3).

name: DNV-ST-B203 Additive manufacturing (Edition 2025-11)
year: 2017 (DNVGL-CG-0197); first ST-B203 edition reported as 2019 (not confirmed); editions Dec 2022 and 2025-11
developer: DNV (formerly DNV GL)
earlier_versions: DNVGL-CG-0197 (2017): class guideline on AM qualification and certification; testing extent set by criticality, no per-category counts; read in full. | DNVGL-ST-B203 Additive manufacturing of metallic parts, first edition (year Unknown): covered two metal AM technologies. | DNV-ST-B203 edition of Dec 2022: added DED-arc, PBF-EB and binder jetting, combined manufacturing, NDT acceptance criteria, and guidance on part families and AMC selection; the 2025-11 edition adds polymers, a CO2 footprint method and grouped part approvals.
description: Assigns parts to AM categories AMC 1–3 by criticality (an informative appendix guides AMC selection). The category sets the qualification route: AMC 1 needs a facility audit and a build process qualification, and AMC 2/3 add part family qualification. Appendices give inspection/test plans and NDT guidance.
NRE_note: The standard requires build process qualification to fix the build process before production, a required parameter-development step, and has an informative appendix on design of AM parts, neither costed as engineering effort (DNV ST-B203 page; DNV slides).
Production_note: The documented scope (procurement, qualification, quality management, production, testing and inspection, plus AMC-selection, design, CO2-footprint, NDT-technology and test-plan appendices) plainly contains no per-part cost estimation (DNV ST-B203 page).
QA_Qual_note: Peron et al. give DNV-ST-B203 qualification requirements by criticality class with test counts (a BPQ of 12 tensile, 3 impact and one each of hardness, microstructure, porosity, chemistry and visual for all classes, plus a part qualification test set for class 3), and DNV's 2022 slides show the AM category sets the steps (AMC 1 facility audit plus BPQ, AMC 2/3 add part family qualification), though both are secondary, cite no edition and differ on which classes need part-level qualification (Peron et al. 2023, Table 2; DNV slides 2022).
QA_Insp_note: Peron et al. set DNV-ST-B203 production testing by class (class 1 visual only; class 2 per-build tensile, impact, visual, surface and volumetric NDT and dimensional check; class 3 adds microstructure, hardness and porosity) and DNV states the standard defines PBF/DED inspection and test plans and NDT acceptance criteria, though the class mapping rests on this secondary source, which cites no edition (Peron et al. 2023, Table 2; DNV 2022 news).
Storage_note: The standard's documented scope has no inventory element; DNV's release mentions storing spares digitally only as a general AM benefit (DNV ST-B203 page; DNV 2022 news).
Shared_Capital_note: Qualification is reused across parts by rule, without numbers: prequalification is per facility, BPQ per material, and part-family guidance 'may extend the validity of qualifications', so prior qualification changes what a new part needs (DNV slides; DNV 2022 news; Peron et al. 2023).
Shared_Capacity_note: The documented scope (procurement, qualification, quality management, production, testing, inspection) does not address print capacity shared across sites or users (DNV ST-B203 page).
Speed_note: The standard has no time or lead-time element; DNV's release mentions lead-time reduction from local manufacturing only as a general AM benefit (DNV ST-B203 page; DNV 2022 news).

name: API Standard 20S Additively Manufactured Metallic Components (AM Specification Levels AMSL 1/2/3)
developer: American Petroleum Institute
description: Specifies process qualification and production control for AM metallic components at three AM Specification Levels. Each higher level raises technical, quality and qualification requirements, and the level is assigned by the product specification, purchaser or manufacturer according to consequence of failure, service severity and inspectability.
NRE_note: The manufacturer must qualify the machine, parameters, feedstock and post-processing (essential AM variables, aligned with ASME IX QW-600 in the 2nd edition) before production, a prescribed parameter-development step with no cost (Inspenet summary; World Oil 2025).
Production_note: The documented scope is qualification of the manufacturing process, production, marking and documentation, which plainly excludes per-part cost estimation; no summary mentions a cost method (GlobalSpec and Normservis scope; Inspenet).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification requirements rise across AMSL 1-3, assigned by consequence of failure, service severity and inspectability, and require representative coupons, mechanical testing and metallography, but per-level test counts could not be verified because the full text is paid (GlobalSpec scope; Inspenet summary).
QA_Insp_note: NDE methods (RT, UT, PT, MT, CT, dimensional) are named, the NDT plan depends on criticality, and the 2nd edition adds an NDT annex on how AMSLs apply with example acceptance criteria, but class-specific inspection scope was not verified (Inspenet; World Oil 2025).
Storage_note: The scope (process qualification, production, marking, documentation) excludes inventory; reduced inventories appear only as motivation in announcements and press (scope listings; World Oil 2025).
Shared_Capital_note: No scope listing, summary or announcement says whether one process qualification can cover several parts or part families, and the paid full text was not accessible (API announcement; GlobalSpec and Normservis scope; Inspenet; World Oil 2025).
Shared_Capacity_note: The documented scope (process qualification, production control, marking, documentation) excludes print capacity shared across sites or users (scope listings).
Speed_note: The requirements scope excludes lead time; API's announcement says only that the standard was developed to help reduce lead time, a motivation rather than a requirement (API announcement; scope listings).

name: FAA AM Roadmap and risk-based certification framework (Gorelik briefings)
developer: Federal Aviation Administration (AM National Team; M. Gorelik, Chief Scientist for Fatigue and Damage Tolerance)
description: Ties regulatory scrutiny to part criticality and maps the qualification path to criticality and volume: point-design certification for low-criticality, high-margin parts; part-family qualification as volume grows; model-enabled qualification later. It gives indicative figures for the barrier to entry and qualification timelines.
NRE_note: Process development is named among the drivers of an indicative barrier-to-entry estimate (about $1M optimistic vs '$10's of M' realistic) as background, and whether the framework uses one-time engineering in any decision cannot be confirmed from the briefing slides (Gorelik 2016 National Academies deck slide 15).
Production_note: Production cost appears only as quoted background (about 50% of operating cost is labour and 20% depreciation; AM F-15 pylon ribs cost 3-5x forgings), and per-part production cost lies outside the scope of a risk-based certification-path framework (Gorelik 2016 deck slide 12; NRC 2017 deck slide 15).
QA_Qual_note: A building-block table gives specimen counts, cost and years per test level (coupons 5,000-100,000 specimens, $8-15M, 2 years, up to full-scale articles) and alloy introduction is put at 10-15 years, while qualification paths are mapped to criticality and volume only qualitatively and no counts are set by part class (Gorelik 2016 deck slides 21, 25; FAA REDAC 2017 roadmap slide 15).
QA_Insp_note: Capable NDI is named a key challenge and POD-based fracture mechanics and a CT and laser-ultrasonics validation task are proposed as research, not inspection requirements the framework applies, and the briefings cannot confirm any decision use (Gorelik 2016 deck; FAA REDAC 2017 roadmap slide 25).
Storage_note: The briefings are a certification and research framework whose scope excludes parts inventory, and none of the decks discusses stock or holding cost, naming aftermarket parts and repairs only as application areas (FAA REDAC 2017 roadmap slide 15; Gorelik 2016 and NRC 2017 decks).
Shared_Capital_note: The framework maps the qualification path to volume, moving to part-family qualification as production volume grows, which spreads qualification across parts, but no numbers are given (FAA REDAC 2017 roadmap slide 15; NRC 2017 deck).
Shared_Capacity_note: Print-capacity pooling lies outside the certification framework's scope, and the decks mention only OEM production ramps and an expanding supply-chain footprint (FAA REDAC 2017 roadmap; NRC 2017 deck slides 8, 21).
Speed_note: The NRC briefing quotes a case in which a Ti-6Al-4V forging had about a one-year lead time and an AM substitute met an urgent depot need, a case result the framework does not compute, and lead-time value lies outside the scope of a certification-path framework (NRC 2017 deck slide 15).

name: CMU adaptive regulatory framework for metal AM in aviation (Bonnín Roca et al. 2017)
developer: Carnegie Mellon University, Engineering and Public Policy (with Universidade de Lisboa / CMU Portugal)
earlier_versions: Bonnín Roca, Fuchs, Morgan & Vaishnav 2016, 'Policy needed for additive manufacturing' (Nature Materials commentary): earlier call for process science, standards and adaptive regulation that the 2017 paper develops into a framework.
description: Uses metal AM in aviation as a case study to propose adaptive regulation: standards revised periodically, and firms regulated differently according to their technological capabilities. It gives a general framework in which the right regulatory design depends on industry structure, safety requirements and sources of technological uncertainty.
NRE_note: Only abstracts were read; the paper concerns regulating the uncertainty of an immature metal AM production process, so whether it discusses process-parameter development or other one-time engineering effort cannot be settled without the paywalled full text (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS and TU/e).
Production_note: Per-part production cost is outside the documented scope of a regulatory-design framework (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS).
QA_Qual_note: The abstract proposes adaptive safety regulation of metal AM, with periodically revised standards and requirements that differ by firm capability, as the authors' policy design rather than a procedure that sets qualification steps; whether the framework applies any qualification rule cannot be confirmed from the abstract (Research Policy 2017 abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only abstracts could be read and they do not mention inspection or NDE requirements, and the full paper and the 2017 CMU dissertation were not reachable, so whether inspection is treated is not established (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS, TU/e and CORE).
Storage_note: Inventory is outside the documented scope of a regulatory-design framework (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS).
Shared_Capital_note: Only abstracts could be read; regulating firms by technological capability might let qualification carry across parts, but no source read shows the paper treating machine cost or qualification reuse (Research Policy 2017 abstract via TU/e and IDEAS).
Shared_Capacity_note: Print capacity pooling is outside the documented scope of a regulatory-design framework (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS).
Speed_note: Part lead time and availability are outside the documented scope of a framework for setting certification regulation (Research Policy 2017 abstract via IDEAS).

name: Rapid qualification framework for powder-bed laser AM parts (Honeywell-led DARPA Open Manufacturing work; Peralta et al.)
developer: Honeywell Aerospace-led team (Peralta, Enright, Megahed, Gong, Roybal, Craig) under DARPA Open Manufacturing
description: A probabilistic, risk-based qualification framework that runs ICME models (melt pool CFD, residual stress/distortion FE, microstructure/strength) with Bayesian calibration in a digital loop, adding physical tests only when the digital results do not show acceptable risk. In-situ monitoring and NDE feed the risk calculation.
NRE_note: ICME process models are run to find the optimum process window, a parameter-development activity the framework performs, but engineering effort is not costed and does not enter the qualification decision (IMMI 2016 full text, Rapid qualification framework).
Production_note: Production cost, machine time and material cost are not addressed anywhere in the full paper (IMMI 2016 full text).
QA_Qual_note: A probabilistic risk framework decides when physical qualification tests are needed, but the 40% time, 20% cost and 40% testing reductions are programme goals, cost-based test prioritisation is only proposed, and no cost model or test counts are given (IMMI 2016 full text).
QA_Insp_note: Pyrometer quality metrics against a 95% limit flag off-nominal layers and NDE (X-ray CT, acoustic microscopy) is said to feed the risk calculation, but no inspection cost, POD, sampling plan or class-based scope is given (IMMI 2016 full text, In-process sensors and NDT sections).
Storage_note: Inventory, stock or spares are not addressed in the full paper (IMMI 2016 full text).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine capital and its sharing are not addressed; the remark on interchangeability of components and AM processes concerns the framework's modularity (IMMI 2016 full text).
Shared_Capacity_note: Printer capacity, throughput and pooling are not addressed (IMMI 2016 full text).
Speed_note: The paper claims rapid qualification enables faster response to market demands and rapid procurement of qualified hardware, but part lead time does not enter the framework (IMMI 2016 full text, Abstract).

name: NIST qualification pathways for AM materials, processes and parts (statistical, equivalence-based, model-based, 'qualify-as-you-go')
year: 2014-2025 (project page created March 2014; project completed; page last updated March 2025)
developer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: Frames three qualification routes with different testing burdens and develops measurement science (round-robin protocols, a public materials database, validated process models, in-process measurement) to make equivalence and model-based qualification viable and to spread the cost of statistical testing.
NRE_note: The documented scope is measurement science to cut the cost and time of qualifying AM materials, processes and parts; part design files and run-parameter development for a given part are outside it and not mentioned (NIST project page).
Production_note: Production cost is outside the documented qualification scope; every cost reference on the page concerns qualification testing (NIST project page).
QA_Qual_note: The project page contrasts the testing burden of statistical, equivalence and model-based routes, quoting full empirical qualification at 'many thousands of individual tests, costing millions of dollars', as background to measurement-science research; whether any pathway prescribes qualification activities as requirements cannot be confirmed from the public summary (NIST project page).
QA_Insp_note: 'Qualify as you go' is described as a concept using pre-, in- and post-process measurements to show each part meets specification; whether it prescribes inspection as a requirement cannot be confirmed from the public summary (NIST project page).
Storage_note: Inventory is plainly outside the documented qualification scope and is not mentioned (NIST project page).
Shared_Capital_note: Round-robin testing protocols and 'a publicly available materials database' are research activities meant to spread qualification cost across contributors, and whether any pathway uses shared data in a decision cannot be confirmed from the public summary (NIST project page).
Shared_Capacity_note: Machine capacity is plainly outside the documented qualification scope and is not mentioned (NIST project page).
Speed_note: Part lead time is outside the documented scope; the only time figure is the 5-15 years of empirical qualification, which concerns qualification duration (NIST project page).

name: Seifi et al. qualification and certification pathway review (JOM, 2017)
developer: Seifi, Salem, Beuth, Harrysson, Lewandowski (2016); Seifi, Gorelik, Waller, Hrabe, Shamsaei, Daniewicz, Lewandowski (2017)
earlier_versions: Seifi et al. 2016, Overview of Materials Qualification Needs for Metal Additive Manufacturing (JOM 68, doi:10.1007/s11837-015-1810-0): companion review; source of the AMS4999A test counts and the 'millions of dollars, up to 15 years' figure.
description: Compares statistically based qualification (e.g., AMS4999A), model-based qualification and ICME 'qualify-as-you-go' schemes for metal AM. The 2017 paper maps the standards landscape needed for a Q&C pathway and cites NASA's AM risk criteria (inspectability, surface removal, wall thickness).
NRE_note: Full 2017 text read: the one-time effort or cost of preparing design files, redesigning parts or developing parameters is not addressed, since the passage on vendors' proprietary optimised process variables concerns obstacles to standards development and 'design for AM' appears only as a topic of other agencies' guidance (NIST copy of JOM 2017, pp. 3, 19).
Production_note: 2017 full text read: part production cost is not addressed, and cost appears only for lengthy and expensive in-house specifications and rapid qualification (NIST copy of JOM 2017, pp. 5, 8).
QA_Qual_note: The 2016 companion review gives costable counts for one statistical route (AMS4999A tensile results per build direction for source and production qualification) and a millions-of-dollars, up-to-15-years legacy qualification estimate, while the 2017 paper maps pathways and standards without counts; no class-specific counts or cost model (JOM 2016 per the earlier full-text reading, not reopenable this round; NIST copy of JOM 2017).
QA_Insp_note: The review discusses NDT as central to mitigating part failure, XCT as the leading technique, part-specific acceptance criteria and NASA's inspectability risk criterion, but it sets no inspection requirement of its own and uses inspection in no decision (NIST copy of JOM 2017, pp. 11-16).
Storage_note: 2017 full text read: spares appear only as items needing defined NDT, and inventory is not addressed (NIST copy of JOM 2017, p. 20).
Shared_Capital_note: Design-allowable and pedigree databases and open-platform machines are discussed as ways to reuse qualification data across users, but the review applies no rule that uses capital sharing (NIST copy of JOM 2017, pp. 16, 19-20).
Shared_Capacity_note: 2017 full text read: shared print capacity is not addressed, the only capacity mention being GE's plan to build 10,000 machines (NIST copy of JOM 2017, p. 2).
Speed_note: Making otherwise unavailable parts on demand in days rather than months is cited as motivation, and lead time enters no step of the pathway (NIST copy of JOM 2017, p. 2).

name: Cost model for the economic evaluation of in-situ monitoring tools in metal AM (Colosimo, Cavalli, Grasso)
developer: Politecnico di Milano
description: A per-part cost model comparing as-is production, in-situ monitoring, and monitoring with diagnosis. It uses scrap fraction, false-alarm and missed-detection rates, inspection time and monitoring equipment cost to find the scrap rates at which monitoring pays off, including a make-or-buy variant.
NRE_note: Build preparation and machine setup are costed per build and divided by parts per build, but CAD development cost is explicitly excluded and there is no parameter-development or redesign term (Polimi author manuscript, Sec. 2.2.3, Eqs. 9-10).
Production_note: Per-part cost is computed from material, pre-process, L-PBF process and post-process terms divided by (1 - scrap fraction), validated within about 10% of a service-bureau benchmark (Polimi author manuscript, Eqs. 1-2, Sec. 4.1).
QA_Qual_note: The full paper models no qualification or certification cost or activity; certified medical materials appear only as background to the dental case (Polimi author manuscript, Sec. 3.1).
QA_Insp_note: Per-part inspection cost (operator plus metrology rate times inspection time, visual or CMM) is a line item, combined with scrap fraction, Type I/II monitoring errors and 50k/150k EUR monitoring hardware to find break-even scrap fractions (Polimi author manuscript, Eq. 15, Sec. 3.1-4.2).
Storage_note: The full paper has no inventory, stock or holding-cost term; the only space cost is floor-space rental inside the machine hourly rate (Polimi author manuscript, Sec. 2.2.3).
Shared_Capital_note: The L-PBF system is charged at an hourly rate from straight-line depreciation of EUR 600k over 5 years at a 55% load factor plus maintenance and space, and build cost is divided by parts per build (8, 4, 2) (Polimi author manuscript, Sec. 3.2, Table 4).
Shared_Capacity_note: In the make-or-buy variant in-house L-PBF capacity is saturated, annual throughput is computed (4,585 vs 4,821 parts/year) and extra demand is outsourced at a higher price, so capacity affects cost only, with no lead-time or service effect and no cross-site pooling (Polimi author manuscript, Sec. 4.3, Eq. 19).
Speed_note: The model computes average production time per part including scrapped builds and annual throughput, but no lead time, delivery or availability (Polimi author manuscript, Eqs. 16-17, Sec. 4.3).

name: Process-based cost estimation model for metal AM spare parts with explicit qualification-test line items (Sheikh et al.)
developer: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (Sheikh, Hadid, Padmanabhan, Elomri, Kerbache, Alabtah, Khraisheh)
description: Total part cost is the sum of design, material, manufacturing (print, debind, sinter), post-processing and 'part qualification' cost. The qualification term sums per-part tests for dimensions, corrosion, strength, hardness and density.
NRE_note: Design cost is an explicit term covering reverse-engineering scan time (scanner cost over annual usage hours), software licence spread over parts and designer time times rate, $80-220 per part in the cases (IEOM full text, Eqs. 2-3, Table 3).
Production_note: Per-part cost is built from material, printing (setup labour, depreciation, maintenance, energy times print time), debinding, sintering and post-processing terms (IEOM full text, Eqs. 1, 4-19).
QA_Qual_note: The 'part qualification' term is a flat per-part lump of five test fees (dimensional $30, corrosion $50, strength $40, hardness $25, density $20), with no material or process qualification campaign, class-based test counts or approval cost (IEOM full text, Eq. 20, Table 3).
QA_Insp_note: Per-part inspection and test costs (dimensional inspection by calipers, micrometers or CMM, plus corrosion, strength, hardness and density tests) are explicit line items totalling $120-165 per part (IEOM full text, Eq. 20, Table 3).
Storage_note: No inventory or stock term appears in any cost equation; inventory is cited only as literature motivation in the introduction (IEOM full text).
Shared_Capital_note: Printer and furnace capital enter as flat depreciation per hour times processing time with no utilisation, batch or volume input; only the 3D scanner is spread over annual usage hours (IEOM full text, Eqs. 3, 7-12).
Shared_Capacity_note: Capacity, batching and distributed production are not modelled, and the conclusion states economies of scale are not accounted for (IEOM full text, Conclusion).
Speed_note: No lead-time, downtime or availability term exists and print and sinter times serve only as cost drivers; lead time and downtime appear only as literature motivation (IEOM full text).

name: ASTM E3166-20e1 Standard Guide for Nondestructive Examination of Metal Additively Manufactured Aerospace Parts After Build
developer: ASTM Committee E07
earlier_versions: ASTM E3166-20 (2020): original edition, now listed as historical; reissued as E3166-20e1 with an editorial change that the ASTM page does not describe.
description: Surveys established and emerging NDT methods (CT, eddy current, optical metrology, penetrant, process-compensated resonance testing, radiography, thermography, ultrasonics) against AM flaw types, with a method-versus-flaw table and factors for selecting methods.
NRE_note: The scope covers post-build NDT methods only and leaves input material control, equipment and manufacturing process to ASTM F42, plainly excluding design and parameter development (ASTM scope page, secs. 1.8, 1.12).
Production_note: The scope is selection and application of NDT methods to AM parts, which plainly excludes per-part production cost (ASTM scope page, sec. 1).
QA_Qual_note: The scope excludes control of input materials, equipment and processes (1.12), fracture-critical part inspection requirements (1.13) and accept-reject criteria (1.14), so material, process and part qualification fall outside it (ASTM scope page).
QA_Insp_note: The guide surveys CT, ET, optical metrology, PT, PCRT, RT, IRT and UT against AM flaw types to inform method selection but states that it recommends no course of action, so it prescribes no inspection as a requirement (ASTM scope page, secs. 1.6, 1.8, 1.11).
Storage_note: Inventory is outside the documented NDT-method scope (ASTM scope page).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine investment and its sharing are outside the documented NDT-method scope (ASTM scope page).
Shared_Capacity_note: Print capacity is outside the documented NDT-method scope (ASTM scope page).
Speed_note: Lead time and availability are outside the documented NDT-method scope (ASTM scope page).

name: In-situ NDE (INDE) with probability-of-detection framework for L-PBF (ORNL; Snow et al.)
developer: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (Snow, Scime, Ziabari, Fisher, Paquit)
description: Detects 200–1000 µm subsurface flaws from fused process-monitoring data using machine learning, with XCT as ground truth, and generates POD/PFA curves and an a90/95 metric following NDE practice, so in-situ monitoring can be assessed as an inspection method.
NRE_note: The documented scope is in-situ detection of subsurface flaws from process-monitoring data validated against XCT, which plainly excludes design-file or parameter-development cost (ORNL abstract).
Production_note: The documented scope is flaw detection and POD/PFA assessment, which plainly excludes per-part production costing (ORNL abstract).
QA_Qual_note: The industry qualification paradigm for critical L-PBF parts and the lack of a POD number for certification are background motivation; whether the method uses part qualification in any decision cannot be confirmed from the abstract (ORNL abstract; EurekAlert release).
QA_Insp_note: The method's output is an inspection decision, flagging subsurface flaws from fused in-situ data and rating detection with POD/PFA curves and an a90/95 metric against XCT, but inspection cost is only claimed as lower than ex-situ XCT, with no cost or time figures (ORNL abstract; EurekAlert release).
Storage_note: The documented scope is an in-process flaw-detection method, which plainly excludes inventory (ORNL abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The documented scope is flaw detection, which plainly excludes machine capital or its sharing (ORNL abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: The documented scope is flaw detection on L-PBF builds, which plainly excludes pooled print capacity (ORNL abstract).
Speed_note: The abstract has no time content, and the release's time remarks concern inspection effort (CT needs extra time and expertise, saving time and money on large assemblies) and how fast the algorithm learns a design, with no claim or calculation of lead time, delivery or part availability (ORNL abstract; EurekAlert release).

name: VEXTEC VPS-MICRO model-assisted AM certification (AFWERX SBIR; AFRL QUASAR)
developer: VEXTEC Corporation
description: Probabilistic microstructure- and defect-based fatigue software. It aims to predict EIDS distributions and part performance from specimen-level data so that part-level testing can be limited to validation ('risk-based certification').
NRE_note: VEXTEC names AM process development as a use of the tool and runs virtual microstructure sensitivity studies across build parameters, claiming cost and time savings; whether parameter-development effort enters any decision of the tool cannot be confirmed from public sources (vextec.com AM page; TRX webinar 2021).
Production_note: VEXTEC says VPS-MICRO can optimise post-build selective machining, which can be up to 20% of part cost, a claimed benefit; whether the tool uses part cost in its decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (vextec.com AM page; AM news feed).
QA_Qual_note: Model-assisted, risk-based certification combines limited physical testing with fatigue simulation to reduce the testing needed to qualify an LPBF sustainment component, but no test count, cost or time reduction is computed or quantified (vextec.com AM page; AFRL news feed; TRX webinar 2021).
QA_Insp_note: The Phase II SBIR topic called for developing a framework linking in-process monitoring and non-destructive evaluation data to VPS-MICRO and the deck names NDE as a cost and lead-time driver, but the demonstrated workflow uses literature material data, so whether inspection enters the tool's decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (TRX webinar 2021, slides 11, 13, 23; vextec.com AM page).
Storage_note: VPS-MICRO predicts fatigue performance risk from material data and FEA geometry, so spare-part inventory is plainly outside its documented scope (vextec.com software page).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine capital and its sharing are outside the documented scope of a fatigue-prediction tool; the deck mentions machine-manufacturer-specific allowables only as a burden of current practice (vextec.com software page; TRX webinar 2021).
Shared_Capacity_note: Print capacity is plainly outside the documented scope of a fatigue-prediction and certification tool (vextec.com software and AM pages).
Speed_note: VEXTEC claims its approach cuts long lead times because testing burden affects 'the schedule and cost of AM part availability', but the tool predicts fatigue performance and lead time is outside its documented scope (VEXTEC AFRL news feed; TRX webinar 2021).

name: NASA-CMU Additive Manufacturing Ecosystem for qualification of AM processes and materials in aviation
developer: NASA Ames Research Center (K. Datta) and Carnegie Mellon University (A. Rollett)
description: A six-project research ecosystem for qualifying AM machines, which then supports certification of part production. It names qualification difficulty and cost as the main barriers.
NRE_note: The 'AM Flaw Management' and 'Qualification Aware Process Maps' projects define processing windows with multiple qualified process-variable points, a parameter-development activity the research performs, with no sign that its effort enters a decision (TechPort data sheet).
Production_note: Technology cost is named as a main barrier, post-processing is said to cost as much as fabrication and lower cost for short-run and replacement parts is a target, but the data sheet shows no cost used in any step (TechPort data sheet).
QA_Qual_note: The NTRS abstract describes a research programme of six projects that will develop an ecosystem for qualifying AM machines to support later part certification, not a qualification procedure or gate the tool applies (NTRS abstract; TechPort data sheet).
QA_Insp_note: The data sheet sets porosity limits and cites synchrotron CT only as research characterisation, and does not say whether per-part inspection is addressed; no project outputs were found (TechPort data sheet).
Storage_note: All six listed projects (flaw management, process maps, post-processing, database analytics, training, scaling to production) concern qualification and production, a scope that plainly excludes inventory, and replacement parts appear only as a cost motivation (TechPort data sheet).
Shared_Capital_note: The ecosystem qualifies AM machines so that qualification supports certification of the parts they make and pools process-structure-property data across members, a description of qualification reuse that enters no decision step shown (NTRS abstract; TechPort data sheet).
Shared_Capacity_note: OEMs are said to plan subcontracting much AM fabrication to small AM contractors, whom the ecosystem trains, and a 'Scaling to Production' project configures cells for hundreds to thousands of parts per year, but no work is assigned across suppliers (TechPort data sheet).
Speed_note: The data sheet claims the work will reduce time-to-production, an expected benefit with no lead time used in any step (TechPort data sheet).

name: 3DXpert (build preparation with print time and cost estimation)
year: Estimation feature documented 2019; 'Cost estimation and reports' still listed Feb 2026
developer: Developed by 3D Systems (TCT ties it to the 2015 Cimatron acquisition). On 1 Oct 2025, 3D Systems agreed to sell 3DXpert and Oqton MOS to Hubb Global Holdings, with closing expected Q4 2025. 3D Systems' FY2025 10-K says it 'divested of the 3DXpert business in 2025'. Feb 2026 product material is issued by Oqton Inc.
description: Metal AM build-prep software (part positioning, supports, lattices, print strategies). Its Estimation Parameters dialog computes print time from published build rates (part/support/lattice rates, recoat time). It then costs material per cm3 and machine time at an hourly rate, reporting volume, time and cost for parts, supports and lattices plus total powder required.
NRE_note: The software performs one-time engineering work (DfAM, topology optimisation, lattices, parametric build preparation, 'Automation, Quotation & Setup'), but the estimation dialog has no preparation, setup or engineering cost field, so NRE does not enter its estimate (2019 estimation guide; oqton.com/3dxpert).
Production_note: Build cost is computed from material cost per cm3 for parts, supports and lattices plus machine time cost (hourly rate x total time from part, support and lattice printing rates and recoat time); labour and post-processing are not included (2019 estimation guide).
QA_Qual_note: The AM Inspection module is offered for first-article printing with an 'Inspect, Adjust, Certify for future comparisons' step that certifies a reference build, a feature that does not enter the time and cost estimate or any qualification decision (oqton.com/3dxpert; 3DXpert Introduction 2026).
QA_Insp_note: Build Inspection is offered to inspect and correct anomalies and defects and to trace part quality against build preparation and simulation, a feature whose cost does not enter the estimation dialog (oqton.com/3dxpert; 3DXpert Introduction 2026; 2019 estimation guide).
Storage_note: 3DXpert is build-preparation software; inventory functions sit in the separate Manufacturing OS/MES products, so inventory is outside its documented scope (oqton.com/3dxpert; 3DXpert Introduction 2026).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine cost enters only as an hourly rate x total build time, with no amortisation, utilisation or per-part allocation of multi-part builds (2019 estimation guide).
Shared_Capacity_note: Documented scope is preparing and estimating individual builds; no fleet, scheduling or multi-site capacity function is described (oqton.com/3dxpert; 3DXpert Introduction 2026).
Speed_note: Print time is estimated from part, support and lattice printing rates plus between-layer recoat time, a print-time-only model; lead time or availability is not computed (2019 estimation guide).

name: Ansys Additive Prep (Cost Estimator)
developer: Ansys, now part of Synopsys (ansys.com product pages redirect to ansys.synopsys.com); Additive Prep runs inside Ansys SpaceClaim
description: Build-preparation tool whose Cost Estimator prices the whole build job. Machine cost comes from build time (laser path and jump times plus recoater time per layer). Material is powder volume over the baseplate area times part height, times density, plus a material-loss %. A profit margin is added. Output is an 'Estimated Total Price' exportable to CSV.
NRE_note: Orientation, supports and scan-pattern build files are prepared in the tool, but that preparation effort is not a cost term and does not enter the Cost Estimator's price (Ansys Additive Prep help 2024 R2).
Production_note: The Cost Estimator prices a build job from scan-path build time times machine cost, powder volume times density plus a loss %, and profit, giving an Estimated Total Price; labour and per-part split are not documented (Ansys help 2024 R2).
QA_Qual_note: The cost-estimator help lists only machine, material and profit terms, and build preparation does not include qualification (Ansys help 2024 R2).
QA_Insp_note: The cost-estimator help lists only machine, material and profit terms, with no inspection step; post-processing appears only as a source of powder loss (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Storage_note: Additive Prep prepares and prices single build jobs, so inventory is outside its documented scope (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine cost (the largest contributor) is charged on build time from the SLM machine profile and covers everything in the build volume, but no amortisation, utilisation or per-part allocation input is documented (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Shared_Capacity_note: Additive Prep prices one build job on one machine and does not address capacity shared across sites or users (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Speed_note: Build time is computed from laser path, jump and recoater times, but only to price machine time; no lead time or value of earlier delivery is output (Ansys help 2024 R2).

name: Ansys Granta Selector (Additive Manufacturing data)
year: Senvol integration announced May 2016; AM Edition in CES Selector 2019; AM data still listed in 2026 R1 help
developer: Granta Design (now Ansys Granta Selector; ansys.com redirects to ansys.synopsys.com); AM machine/material data from Senvol LLC
earlier_versions: CES Selector with Senvol data (May 2016): Granta Design first integrated Senvol machine and material data (550+ machines, 700+ materials) into CES Selector and GRANTA MI. | CES Selector 2019 Additive Manufacturing Edition (2019): Granta Design release covering >950 AM machines, >1,700 materials and >190 conventional equivalents from the updated Senvol Database; now sold as Ansys Granta Selector.
description: Materials/process selection software. The AM Edition embeds Senvol machine and material data. Users can filter machines by process, manufacturer, required part size, cost and compatible materials, and chart AM properties against conventional equivalents to judge whether AM is viable. A generic Part Cost Estimator gives relative costs (+/-20%) across processes, but AM coverage is not documented.
NRE_note: The help documents a materials and process selection database (Senvol machine/material records and AM test data) plus a relative part-cost estimator; redesign, digitisation and parameter development are outside that documented scope (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
Production_note: The Part Cost Estimator computes relative part cost (+/-20%) from material, mass, batch size, load factor, write-off time, overhead rate and a process record, but the help says only processes 'with data to support' it are shown and never says AM processes are among them (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
QA_Qual_note: The AM data supply tensile, creep, fatigue and fracture test data for Ni and Ti AM alloys as selection data, but the tool does not gate, plan or cost qualification, which is outside its documented selection scope (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
QA_Insp_note: The documented selection data and cost-estimator inputs contain no per-part inspection or NDT item (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
Storage_note: Materials and process selection with relative part costing; no inventory or stock feature appears in the help pages read (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
Shared_Capital_note: AM machines can be filtered and compared by cost as a selection criterion, and the Part Cost Estimator writes off non-dedicated capital with a load factor, but its coverage of AM processes is not documented, so for AM only the machine-cost filter is shown (3DPI 2016; Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
Shared_Capacity_note: No capacity, site or network feature appears in the help; production capacity is outside the materials-selection scope (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).
Speed_note: The AM data page names no lead time or build rate and the cost estimator outputs cost only; lead time is outside the selection scope (Granta Selector help 2026 R1).

name: Ansys Granta MI:Additive Manufacturing
developer: Granta Design (acquired by Ansys; ansys.com product pages now redirect to ansys.synopsys.com)
description: Enterprise database package for AM data. It stores process parameters and logged build data, links supplier information to material batches, and exports properties to simulation. Since 2016 it also exposes the Senvol machine/material database next to a company's own AM data for search and comparison.
NRE_note: The 2017 update links material properties to process parameters so users can adjust settings, a feature supporting parameter development, and whether engineering effort enters any decision cannot be confirmed from press sources (TenLinks 2017).
Production_note: The 2015 and 2017 releases describe data capture with no per-part cost, and the Sandia schema layout shows only a bare 'Cost' heading in a machine/material record whose contents are not shown, so whether part cost is held or computed cannot be settled from press and slides (CIMdata 2015; TenLinks 2017; Sandia slides).
QA_Qual_note: The package is positioned to support qualification and certification of AM parts and can generate automated qualification reports, a reporting feature, and whether qualification enters any decision cannot be confirmed from press sources (CIMdata 2015; TenLinks 2017).
