description: Framework to catalogue part suitability across operational, commercial, legal and technical areas and assess part catalogues at scale using vessel and supply chain data, starting with Austal-designed vessels.
NRE_note: The project (1 Jun 2026 to 31 Dec 2027) has published no outputs, and the project page and press name only four assessment areas without saying whether redesign or technical-data effort is assessed (AMCRC page; AM Media).
Production_note: 'Commercial' is one of four areas the framework will catalogue, but the framework is still being developed (June 2026 to December 2027) and the area's criteria are not defined, so whether cost enters the suitability decision cannot be confirmed from public sources (AMCRC page; AM Media).
QA_Qual_note: 'Legal' is one of four planned assessment areas, but its criteria are not defined, so whether qualification or certification gates suitability cannot be confirmed from public sources (AMCRC page; AM Media).
QA_Insp_note: No outputs exist and neither the project page nor the press mentions inspection (AMCRC page; AM Media; Janes).
Storage_note: The framework will use vessel and supply-chain data and aims at supply resilience, but no source says inventory or stock is assessed (AMCRC page; Janes).
Shared_Capital_note: Aggregating AM demand across programs to give industry 'a clear demand signal to support technology investment decisions' is the project's rationale, not a rule that uses capital sharing to decide, and the planned method cannot be confirmed from public sources (AMCRC page; AM Media).
Shared_Capacity_note: Press notes that private AM capacity investment lags because demand is sporadic, but no source says the framework treats pooled capacity or its effect on lead time (Janes).
Speed_note: Shorter lead times and fewer and shorter maintenance periods are claimed benefits, and whether the framework uses lead time to assess parts cannot be confirmed from public sources (AMCRC page; Janes).

name: SNCF AM part identification for a qualified digital inventory (with 3YOURMIND)
developer: SNCF with 3YOURMIND
description: Assessment of economic and technical part data (relevance, cost, production time, materials, qualifications, traceability) to spot AM-ready parts for a qualified digital inventory.
NRE_note: 3D files are a listed screening parameter, so CAD availability acts as a flag, but digitisation is not costed (3YOURMIND SNCF case).
Production_note: Cost of the part is a screening parameter and savings are claimed without figures or a cost model (3YOURMIND SNCF case).
QA_Qual_note: The software is used to 'identify and qualify AM parts according to the right materials and processes' and 3YOURMIND's general framework lists qualifications among assessed part data, but the SNCF sources do not show qualification used as a screening criterion (3YOURMIND SNCF case; 3YOURMIND 2021 qualified digital inventory article; Metal AM 2021).
QA_Insp_note: Only vendor and trade articles describe the work, and none mention inspection or testing (3YOURMIND SNCF case; Metal AM 2021).
Storage_note: Recurrence of use is a screening parameter and the work feeds a digitally qualified inventory said to cut the cost of a heavy physical inventory, without quantification (3YOURMIND SNCF case; 3Dnatives 2021).
Shared_Capital_note: Only vendor and trade articles describe the work, and none mention machine investment or sharing (Metal AM 2021; 3YOURMIND SNCF case).
Shared_Capacity_note: One article says a part can be printed locally instead of waiting for a supplier, but no source describes pooled capacity or a printing network as part of SNCF's assessment (3Dnatives 2021).
Speed_note: Order constraints are a screening parameter and the assessment asks 'How long does it take to produce?', while an 85% cut in AM part delivery time (2.5 months to 10 days) is a vendor-reported case result, not computed by the method (3YOURMIND SNCF case; 3YOURMIND 2021 SNCF article).

name: AM4Rail AM potential assessment pipeline, knowledge graph and dashboard
developer: Fraunhofer Austria (coordinator), Fraunhofer IAPT, VRVis, OeBB Technische Services, Wiener Linien, Wien Energie
decision_levels: Part selection; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Data pipeline that extracts content from technical drawings (image processing, OCR, text mining), links it with ERP/usage data in a knowledge graph, and feeds an economic, ecological and technological life-cycle assessment into an AM potential dashboard. It includes a two-stage sharing-economy concept for jointly used AM infrastructure ('3D Hub Vienna').
NRE_note: The pipeline extracts missing information from existing technical drawings for the assessment, but no source says whether design, digitisation or reverse-engineering effort for production is assessed, and the paper full text is not open (FFG record; VRVis; TESConf abstract).
Production_note: An economic, ecological and technological life-cycle assessment feeds a dashboard saying whether printing is economically worthwhile per part, but the cost inputs are not published (FFG record; VRVis; Fraunhofer newsletter).
QA_Qual_note: The technology assessment checks component requirements such as 'strength, stability or fire protection' and the knowledge graph uses a criticality criterion, screening gates with no qualification steps or cost (VRVis news; TESConf 2024 abstract).
QA_Insp_note: No source says whether per-part inspection is considered in the assessment; the newsletter mentions only that some printed components were tested for weather resistance during the project (FFG record; VRVis; Fraunhofer newsletter).
Storage_note: The project aims to cut storage stages through make-to-order and claims up to 30% savings from choosing the most efficient spare-parts strategy; whether the pipeline uses stock or demand to decide cannot be confirmed from public sources (FFG record; VRVis; TESConf 2024 abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: A two-stage sharing-economy concept proposes jointly used AM infrastructure among the partners; whether the assessment pipeline uses capital sharing in its decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (FFG record; VRVis).
Shared_Capacity_note: The concept starts with a jointly used '3D-Hub Vienna' among consortium partners; whether the pipeline assigns work to it or uses its capacity in decisions cannot be confirmed from public sources (FFG record).
Speed_note: The project expects print-on-demand to 'reduce breakdown and downtime by up to 10 percent', a project target; whether the pipeline uses lead time or downtime in its assessment cannot be confirmed from public sources (VRVis news; FFG record).

name: AM2Scale data-driven ecological and economic decision support for decentralised AM spares
developer: Fraunhofer Austria (coordinator), Fraunhofer IAPT, VRVis, Wien Energie, Wiener Linien, Wiener Netze, OeBB Technische Services
description: Follow-on to AM4Rail to scale decentralised AM spare part supply with 3D reconstruction of parts, a digital warehouse of component twins with a digital product passport, real-time process monitoring, and data-driven economic/ecological decision support; targets 20% lower storage, transport and life-cycle cost.
NRE_note: 3D reconstruction of spare parts is a project objective, an activity the project performs, and whether its effort enters the planned decision support cannot be confirmed from the project record (FFG project record).
Production_note: The summary calls AM spares 'kostengünstig' and plans economic decision support, but no inputs are described, so whether production cost enters decisions cannot be confirmed (FFG project record).
QA_Qual_note: Only the FFG summary is public; it covers reproducibility, process monitoring and a product passport but does not say whether part or process qualification is addressed (FFG project record).
QA_Insp_note: In-process monitoring for quality assurance is a project objective with a 20-50% scrap-rate reduction target, but whether inspection enters the decision support cannot be confirmed from the project record (FFG project record).
Storage_note: A digital warehouse of component twins is planned and a 20% cut in storage, transport and life-cycle costs is targeted, a goal not shown to be computed or used in any decision (FFG project record).
Shared_Capital_note: Only the FFG summary is public; it mentions decentralised production at several sites but not machine investment or sharing (FFG project record).
Shared_Capacity_note: Decentralised production of spares 'an verschiedenen Standorten' is an objective, a production network described without any rule assigning work, so use of shared capacity cannot be confirmed (FFG project record).
Speed_note: The summary says missing spares cause expensive standstills that on-demand AM should avoid, a claim, and whether the decision support uses lead time or downtime cannot be confirmed (FFG project record).

name: IOGP JIS02 digital inventory framework for AM spare parts
developer: IOGP Joint Industry Sprint (Baker Hughes, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, Woodside, Equinor, TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil, Petrobras, Saudi Aramco, Petronas, Shell, ADNOC, Eni)
description: Industry sprint to produce a unified specification and digital inventory framework for 3D-printed oil and gas components and to define what counts as a digital spare part.
NRE_note: The sprint grades components by Digital Readiness Levels from basic scan data (DRL 1) to a complete digital package (DRL 3) and names the work of turning a 3D scan into a printable file, a data-readiness flag with no effort or cost (EDI Weekly c. 2026, describing IOGP JIS02).
Production_note: Cost appears only in words (digital inventory as 'cost-effective') and in a planned one-click RFQ that would send ready packages to qualified suppliers for quotes, so no cost is shown entering a decision (IOGP workshop post; EDI Weekly c. 2026).
QA_Qual_note: The sprint addresses industry standard gaps for AM components and its readiness levels require material test results (from DRL 1), so qualification data is a condition of the grade, with no qualification steps or counts; sending packages only to qualified suppliers belongs to the planned RFQ (IOGP workshop post; EDI Weekly c. 2026).
QA_Insp_note: The highest readiness level (DRL 3) requires a complete digital package including inspection protocols and surface roughness specifications, so inspection is a required element of the grade, without scope or cost (EDI Weekly c. 2026, describing IOGP JIS02).
Storage_note: A document standardising the digital inventory framework and a definition of digital spare parts are planned deliverables aimed at faster digital inventory adoption; whether the framework uses stock in any decision cannot be confirmed (IOGP workshop post, 2024).
Shared_Capital_note: Neither the IOGP posts nor the trade article mention machine investment or its sharing, and no JIS02 deliverable is public (IOGP workshop post; EDI Weekly c. 2026).
Shared_Capacity_note: The framework aims at collaboration across 13 operators and a planned one-click RFQ would send ready packages to qualified suppliers, a planned procurement step that assigns no capacity (IOGP workshop post; EDI Weekly c. 2026).
Speed_note: The planned RFQ workflow is claimed to eliminate weeks of administrative back-and-forth, a claimed time saving; whether lead time enters any decision cannot be confirmed (EDI Weekly c. 2026, describing IOGP JIS02).

name: 3YOURMIND Distributed Manufacturing
year: Launch year not confirmed (company founded 2014); sold as ERP + MES before being renamed Distributed Manufacturing in 2024
developer: 3YOURMIND GmbH
earlier_versions: 3YOURMIND ERP + MES (Order Management) (before 2024): earlier name of the order and production management software; 3YOURMIND's Jan 2025 FAQ says Distributed Manufacturing was 'formerly known as ERP + MES', and the 2025 review dates the renaming to 2024.
description: Order intake, instant quoting with customizable pricing formulas, job scheduling and machine connectivity, with the ability to route orders to internal facilities or invited contract manufacturers. It is execution software that consumes the digital inventory built in Part Identification.
NRE_note: The FAQ and product page describe quoting, scheduling and job tracking but do not say whether engineering, digitisation or build-prep effort is costed (3YOURMIND FAQ; product page).
Production_note: Instant quotes apply the customer's own pricing formulas to data extracted from uploaded 3D files, quoting with partly documented inputs and no documented process cost model (3YOURMIND FAQ).
QA_Qual_note: The FAQ says Distributed Manufacturing serves organisations that produce qualified AM parts, but does not say whether the software tracks, gates or costs qualification (3YOURMIND FAQ).
QA_Insp_note: Job documentation forms record part quality and job parameters and Markforged build reports with sensor data are imported automatically, data recorded rather than used to decide, and press sources cannot confirm any decision use (3YOURMIND FAQ).
Storage_note: Orders draw on the digital inventory built in Part Identification and the vendor claims up to 75% lower inventories, a marketing claim, and whether stock enters any decision in this module cannot be confirmed (3YOURMIND FAQ; home page).
Shared_Capital_note: Jobs are scheduled on connected machines, nested jobs are imported via CSV and the product page claims to 'maximize machine utilization', but whether machine cost or sharing enters any decision cannot be confirmed from public sources (3YOURMIND FAQ; product page).
Shared_Capacity_note: The scheduler tracks machine occupancy and suggests the next free slot, and orders can go to internal facilities or invited contract manufacturers, but no source shows occupancy setting the quoted delivery time or pooling across platforms (direct links planned for 2026) (3YOURMIND FAQ).
Speed_note: The FAQ says the software calculates a delivery timeline for each quote from customer-configured data and finishing times, a computed lead-time output, though it is not tied to the machine schedule and not valued (3YOURMIND FAQ).

name: DigiPart (IDENTIFY / CATALOG / PRINT) with Theia 2D-to-3D
year: Launch year not confirmed (SP3D software in development by Jan 2019; DigiPart in use by Oct 2020; Theia beta Mar 2024)
developer: Spare Parts 3D (SP3D), founded 2015, Singapore/Paris
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: ML software that screens spare-part catalogs (works without drawings, on partial ERP-type data such as part value, MOQ, lead time) for printability and business sense, recommends material/process, builds a digital catalog and connects to local print providers. Theia converts 2D drawings to 3D models.
NRE_note: Theia automates 2D-to-3D digitisation, which SP3D claims cuts conversion from days to minutes and lowers its cost, but whether digitisation effort or drawing availability enters DigiPART's screening cannot be confirmed from public sources (3DPI Theia 2024).
Production_note: The business-case tool filters parts on value, minimum order quantity and lead time and recommends a technology and material, but no per-part AM cost calculation is documented (3DPI Braskem 2020; AMTIL).
QA_Qual_note: DigiPART Passport applies qualification workflow templates matched to criticality class (AMC1 low to AMC3 high) and locks test reports at validation, a criticality-based gate with no qualification cost or effort computed (SP3D Digital Inventory page).
QA_Insp_note: Each part's passport requires NDT reports and test reports as certification data for validation, but inspection is not costed and no class-specific inspection scope is shown (SP3D Digital Inventory page).
Storage_note: DigiPART screens catalogue and stock data, including minimum order quantity, and builds a digital catalogue, with SP3D claiming a 30% cut in spare-parts inventory value, but no holding cost or stock level is output (SP3D Digital Inventory page; 3DPI Braskem 2020).
Shared_Capital_note: DigiPART helped one customer judge whether printing should be in-house or outsourced based on quantity, but no source says whether machine investment or utilisation is costed (AMTIL).
Shared_Capacity_note: Approved parts can be produced internally or sent to SP3D's network of 123+ qualified providers in 25 countries and the software helps judge by quantity whether to print in-house or outsource, but it is not shown assigning or routing work across providers, which public sources cannot confirm (SP3D Digital Inventory page; AMTIL).
Speed_note: Lead time is a screening input (Braskem) and a business-case goal (Ocyan), and faster lead times are claimed, but lead time is not computed or valued (3DPI Braskem 2020; Metal AM Ocyan; SP3D page).

name: Ivaldi Group digital parts platform
developer: Ivaldi Group (San Leandro, California, per 2022 coverage)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Selects, digitizes and verifies spare parts into a digital warehouse ('envelope' of manufacturing/performance data), recommends what should be printed, and routes production to a network of certified local producers, letting customers weight time, cost and carbon.
NRE_note: Parts not in the library can be submitted as 2D drawings or simple sketches, which Ivaldi converts into printable 3D models, a service offered, and whether NRE enters any platform decision cannot be confirmed from press (sap.io platform article; Cloud Wars).
Production_note: Customers weight time, cost and carbon in routing production among 3D printing, injection moulding and CNC, so cost is a weighted factor, but no per-part cost inputs or method are documented and the one-tenth-price clip is a case figure (Cloud Wars; 3DPrint.com 2018).
QA_Qual_note: Every digitised part goes through quality control and physical and algorithmic verification, production solutions are certified and print sources are certified, but qualification effort or cost is not modelled (Cloud Wars; Fabbaloo 2019).
QA_Insp_note: The only inspection-like text is a homepage image caption and a company ISO 9001 quality-policy footer, while the Cloud Wars verification line describes the selection and digitisation process, so no source shows that produced parts are inspected or tested (Ivaldi homepage; Cloud Wars).
Storage_note: A digital library of spare-part models replaces physical stock and the company claims building to order is cheaper than holding inventory, and although its software analyses spare-part inventories for digitisation, whether stock or demand is used to decide cannot be confirmed from press (Fabbaloo 2019; sap.io profile; 3D Printing Industry 2025).
Shared_Capital_note: No source read says whether machine investment, amortisation or utilisation is considered; the 2018 Wilhelmsen pilot facility serving several partners is a business arrangement, not a documented tool function (3DPrint.com 2018; Cloud Wars).
Shared_Capacity_note: Orders are routed to a network of about 15,000 local manufacturers, with a Material-Technology-Location feature showing technologies and materials available by location, but no capacity or queue model is described (sap.io platform article; Cloud Wars).
Speed_note: Time is a priority customers can weight, and a welding-mask clip delivered in 24 hours instead of 3-4 weeks is quoted as a case, but no lead time is computed (Cloud Wars; 3DPrint.com 2018).

name: Materialise OnSite (instant quote portal)
developer: Materialise NV (manufacturing service)
description: Upload a file, choose technology, material, finish and quantity, and receive an instant price and lead-time/shipping-date estimate, usable as an external benchmark for buy-side decisions.
NRE_note: The pages say a quote follows file upload instantly but give no fee breakdown, so whether design, file-repair or setup fees are included is not shown (Materialise OnSite page).
Production_note: The portal returns an instant price for the uploaded geometry and chosen technology, material and finish, but it is a supplier price with an undocumented cost structure (Materialise reseller page; OnSite page).
QA_Qual_note: Projects needing additional certifications are routed to the sales and engineering team outside the instant quote, so qualification is outside the portal's documented scope (Materialise OnSite page).
QA_Insp_note: A limited dimensional inspection report is available on request, a service offered, but whether it enters the instant quote cannot be confirmed from public sources (Materialise OnSite page).
Storage_note: OnSite is an ordering portal for prototypes, models and low-volume runs, a documented scope that excludes inventory holding (Materialise OnSite page).
Shared_Capital_note: Instant prices embed Materialise's machine costs, but the pages do not show how machine capital is allocated (Materialise OnSite page).
Shared_Capacity_note: The portal quotes and ships orders from Materialise's own production and has no capacity or network function beyond a marketing reference to its production capacity (Materialise OnSite page).
Speed_note: The quote interface gives an instant estimate of how long the order will take for any technology, material and finish, and orders in production show an estimated shipment date, so lead time is computed and reported (Materialise reseller page; OnSite page).

name: Paperless Parts (additive manufacturing estimating)
developer: Paperless Parts, Inc.
description: Quoting platform whose AM module analyzes part files for support volume, material volume and orientation, computes runtimes and parts per build, and feeds automated pricing and digital quotes.
NRE_note: The platform-wide pricing page mentions setup time and run time as costing variables drawn from historical data without naming any process, and the AM page lists support volume, material volume, orientation, runtime and parts per build but no setup, build preparation or engineering charge, so AM NRE cannot be established (Paperless Parts pricing and AM pages).
Production_note: The AM module analyses the part file for support volume, material volume and orientation, calculates runtimes and parts per build, and feeds pricing formulas that mark up labour, materials and overhead, so per-part AM cost is computed from geometry, material and machine time (Paperless Parts AM page; pricing and costing page).
QA_Qual_note: The AM and pricing pages do not mention qualification, and the help-centre articles could not be rendered, so this cannot be established (Paperless Parts AM page; llms.txt index).
QA_Insp_note: No page read mentions inspection or quality operations, though job-shop quotes can carry them as operations; the help-centre articles could not be rendered (Paperless Parts AM and pricing pages; llms.txt index).
Storage_note: Paperless Parts quotes and prices jobs for a contract manufacturer, so spare-part inventory is plainly outside its documented scope (Paperless Parts pricing and costing page).
Shared_Capital_note: The AM analysis computes the number of parts per build, which spreads build runtime across parts, but no machine capital, depreciation or utilisation input is documented (Paperless Parts AM page).
Shared_Capacity_note: Paperless Parts prices jobs for one shop's own operations, so capacity pooled across sites or users is outside its documented scope (Paperless Parts AM and pricing pages).
Speed_note: The AM module calculates build runtimes from the part file, a partial time model, but lead-time quoting could not be confirmed because the Dynamic Lead Times help article did not render (Paperless Parts AM page; llms.txt index).

name: Schröder et al. AM cost-structure / PSS cost-calculation model
developer: M. Schröder, B. Falk, R. Schmitt (RWTH Aachen, WZL)
description: Activity-based model that breaks an AM order into eight main process steps and seven cost categories: design and planning, material, machine setup, manufacturing, post-processing, quality, and administration/sales. Build time is computed from build-envelope and part dimensions using 2D/3D packing.
NRE_note: Design and planning ('Konstruktion & Planung') is a separately costed category, EUR 300.18 (24.64%) of the EUR 1,218.27 example order, and the review notes it was among the first AM models to cost design and planning as a distinct activity (IPSS 2015 slides; Khanna et al. 2024).
Production_note: Each process step has its own cost function computed from company data (77 inputs), giving material, setup, manufacturing and post-processing costs per unit with a +/-10% sensitivity analysis (IPSS 2015 slides; Khanna et al. 2024).
QA_Qual_note: Only the slides and reviews are readable (the paper's open copy was unreachable); they cost a 'quality characteristics' category and propose a cost-benefit analysis of quality investments without defining them, so whether qualification is included is not shown (IPSS 2015 slides).
QA_Insp_note: 'Quality check' is one of the costed process steps and appears as a per-unit line item ('Qualitaetsmerkmale', EUR 298.56, 24.51%) in the example order (IPSS 2015 slides; Khanna et al. 2024).
Storage_note: The model costs an AM order, and its complete seven-category unit-cost breakdown summing to EUR 1,218.27 contains no inventory or holding cost (IPSS 2015 slides; Khanna et al. 2024).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine 'investment costs & workload' are the main machine cost factors, and maximum parts per build (Nmax 2D/3D packing) and build-chamber fill level are inputs, so capital is spread with load and multi-part-build assumptions; economies of scale appear only for small parts (IPSS 2015 slides).
Shared_Capacity_note: Machine workload (utilisation) is a named input that drives the machine cost, but it has no effect on lead time and there is no pooling across sites or users (IPSS 2015 slides).
Speed_note: The slides give a formula for machine (build) time from setup, recoating and number of builds and use time inputs only in the unit-cost sensitivity analysis, with no time value or lead time shown, and the paper itself could not be read (IPSS 2015 slides).

name: Knofius-van der Heijden-Zijm AHP spare-part screening (SINTAS; Fokker, Royal Netherlands forces)
developer: N. Knofius, M. C. van der Heijden, W. H. M. Zijm (University of Twente)
description: Two-level AHP. Company goals (secure supply, reduce downtime, reduce costs) weight part attributes that can be pulled from company databases: safety-stock cost, manufacturing/order cost, demand rate, survival probability, remaining usage period, resupply lead time and airplane type. Go/no-go gates on material and size come first, and the ranking tells the firm which parts to build AM business cases for.
NRE_note: The method uses a company keyword for whether the firm holds a part's design rights as an indicator, because design rights mean lower AM setup costs, i.e. design-data availability used as a proxy, with no engineering cost computed (Knofius 2019 thesis, Sec. 2.2.1).
Production_note: Conventional manufacturing/order cost is a scored attribute (17%) used as a proxy for AM savings potential, but no AM cost is estimated (Knofius 2019 thesis, Tables 2.1, 2.5).
QA_Qual_note: Certification is not an attribute or gate; the validation only mentions that practitioners might have dismissed a fitting stud for its high certification costs, so certification does not enter the ranking (Knofius 2019 thesis, Sec. 2.3.1).
QA_Insp_note: Chapter 2 read in full: inspection and quality testing are neither attributes nor gates and are not discussed (Knofius 2019 thesis, Ch. 2).
Storage_note: Safety-stock cost is the highest-weighted attribute (18%) and demand rate (16%) is scored, so stock and demand are screening criteria, but there is no inventory model (Knofius 2019 thesis, Table 2.5).
Shared_Capital_note: Chapter 2 read in full: AM machines appear only as data sheets for feasible size and material ranges, and machine investment or sharing is not discussed (Knofius 2019 thesis, Sec. 2.2.3).
Shared_Capacity_note: Chapter 2 read in full: print capacity, sites and pooling are not discussed; supply options concern alternative sources such as dismantled aircraft (Knofius 2019 thesis, Secs. 2.2, 2.3.1).
Speed_note: Resupply lead time (13%) is a scored attribute under the 'reduce downtime' and 'secure supply' goals, a screening criterion, but downtime or lead time is not computed (Knofius 2019 thesis, Tables 2.3, 2.5).

name: Chaudhuri et al. design-science spare-part selection (TOPSIS + clustering + AHP)
developer: A. Chaudhuri, H. A. Gerlich, J. Jayaram, A. Ghadge, J. Shack, B. H. Brix, L. H. Hoffbeck, N. Ulriksen
description: Database filters (size, time to stock-out, overhead cost, obsolescence, unit cost), then two-step cluster analysis and AHP ranking of clusters with weights from a management workshop (service 72%, cost 22%, other 6%). Parts are ranked with TOPSIS within clusters and finally reviewed against technical drawings.
NRE_note: Availability of technical drawings acted as a gate in the final technical review (only 54 drawings could be obtained for 100 sampled parts), a TDP-availability proxy with no digitisation or redesign cost (Chaudhuri et al., sec. 4.4.5).
Production_note: Unit (standard) cost is used as a filter (1,000 DKK threshold) and an AHP sub-weight, with no AM cost estimate and a business case left as a next step (Chaudhuri et al., secs. 4.1, 4.2, 4.4.5).
QA_Qual_note: Full text read: certification, qualification and testing are not criteria or steps, and quality appears only as a weighted service objective (Chaudhuri et al., secs. 4.1, 4.4.5).
QA_Insp_note: Full text read: inspection or testing of printed parts is not addressed, 'inspection' referring only to manual review of drawings (Chaudhuri et al., sec. 4.4.2).
Storage_note: Calculated per-part overhead cost (covering inventory holding and transport) is a numeric TOPSIS ranking input, alongside inventory-cost and obsolescence AHP weights and a time-to-stock-out filter, but AM's effect on stock or holding cost is not output (Chaudhuri et al., secs. 4.1-4.3).
Shared_Capital_note: Full text read: machine investment, ownership or sharing is not part of the method, with machine cost appearing only in the literature review and TCO models named as future work (Chaudhuri et al., secs. 2.1.2, 5.2).
Shared_Capacity_note: Full text read: print capacity, pooling or production networks are not addressed, and service providers are named only as part-selection software (Chaudhuri et al., sec. 5.3).
Speed_note: Current supply lead time in days is a numeric TOPSIS input (ideal 144 days; 10-57 days for the nine recommended parts) that shapes the ranking output, and availability is weighted 51% within service, but AM lead time is never computed or valued (Chaudhuri et al., secs. 4.1, 4.3, Table 8).

name: McGill automated AM part-candidate decision support (Yang, Page, Zhang & Zhao 2020)
developer: T. D. Page, S. Yang, Y. Zhang, Y. F. Zhao (McGill University)
earlier_versions: Page, Yang & Zhao, 'Automated Candidate Detection for Additive Manufacturing: A Framework Proposal', ICED 2019 (doi:10.1017/dsi.2019.72): framework proposal comparing six classifiers on ~120 expert-labelled parts; all ratings in this entry rest on this paper's full text, as the 2020 JIM article (which extends it toward a decision-support system) was not readable.
description: Machine-learning decision model (a decision tree, best of six sklearn classifiers). It combines ERP economic data (production cost, batch size, inventory cost, import/export, sole-sourcing), CAD complexity ratios and user-answered AM-potential questions to flag economic feasibility and six AM potentials for expert review.
NRE_note: The tool flags AM potentials (lightweighting, functional integration, internal channels) as redesign opportunities for expert review, but redesign or file-preparation effort is not an input to its decision (ICED 2019 full text, Sec. 3.1.2, 4.3).
Production_note: The classifier takes the part's ERP production cost ($/part) as one feature of its economic-feasibility decision, but no AM unit cost is entered or built up by the tool; the SolidWorks Costing machining-vs-AM estimates were used to form the case's feasibility labels (ICED 2019 full text, Table 2, Sec. 4.1.1).
QA_Qual_note: The ICED 2019 full description of the framework was read and qualification or certification is not a criterion ('qualifying a part' in Table 1 refers only to a supplier scenario); the 2020 JIM extension could only be read as an abstract (ICED 2019 full text, Tables 1-2).
QA_Insp_note: The ICED 2019 full text was read; inspection is not a criterion, and surface finish and fatigue are explicitly set aside as too abstract for initial screening (ICED 2019 full text, Sec. 3.1.5).
Storage_note: Inventory cost ($, from ERP) is a numeric input to the economic-feasibility classifier, chosen because AM lowers demand on inventory backlog, but holding cost or AM's effect on stock is not output (ICED 2019 full text, Table 2, Sec. 3.1.3).
Shared_Capital_note: The ICED 2019 full text was read; machine investment or utilisation is not among the final criteria, with 'capacity utilization' only a label in the initial brainstorm figure (ICED 2019 full text, Fig. 2, Table 2).
Shared_Capacity_note: The ICED 2019 full text was read and capacity sharing is not addressed (ICED 2019 full text).
Speed_note: Lead time is a selected economic criterion entered as a value (30 and 40 days in the examples) that, with production cost, forms the economic-feasibility decision, but lead time is not computed or valued (it is listed in Sec. 3.1.3 though missing from Table 2) (ICED 2019 full text, Sec. 3.1.3, 4.1.1, Tables 4 and 6).

name: Yang & Zhao lifecycle part-count-reduction (consolidation) method
developer: S. Yang, Y. F. Zhao (McGill University)
description: Treats part consolidation as a combinatorial optimization that minimizes the lifecycle cost/performance ratio under manufacturing, maintenance and recycling constraints. It is solved with a two-level grouping-and-refinement framework plus part-count-reduction design rules.
NRE_note: The method offers part-count-reduction design rules and a two-level grouping-and-refinement redesign framework, so redesign is what it does, but the abstract does not show redesign effort entering the cost/performance objective (JMD featured-article abstract).
Production_note: The optimisation minimises a lifecycle cost/performance ratio under manufacturing constraints, and part-count reduction is said to cut assembly cost while raising manufacturing difficulty, but the abstract shows no per-part production cost build-up (JMD featured-article abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Only the featured-article abstract was reachable, and it does not say whether qualification enters the lifecycle cost/performance objective (JMD featured-article abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract was reachable, and it does not say whether inspection is part of the lifecycle cost (JMD featured-article abstract).
Storage_note: Only the abstract was reachable; inventory is not mentioned, though maintenance constraints and the irreplaceability of failed subcomponents make spares effects plausibly in scope (JMD featured-article abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: Only the abstract was reachable, and it does not say whether machine cost or build packing enters the manufacturing term (JMD featured-article abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: Outside the documented scope: the method optimises which components of one assembly to consolidate, which does not involve printer capacity pooled across sites or users (JMD featured-article abstract).
Speed_note: Only the abstract was reachable; maintenance is a constraint, but it does not say whether downtime or lead time is valued (JMD featured-article abstract).

name: Ghiasian et al. (2020) preference-based AM design-readiness assessment
developer: S. E. Ghiasian, P. Jaiswal, R. Rai, K. Lewis (University at Buffalo)
earlier_versions: Ghiasian, Jaiswal, Rai, Lewis (2018), ASME IDETC DETC2018-86238 (doi:10.1115/DETC2018-86238): voxel-based fabrication-feasibility framework (geometry, build orientation and supports, resource cost and time) tested on 34 parts; the 2020 version adds multi-criteria readiness scoring with physical-programming preference functions.
description: Voxel-based framework that judges AM feasibility on geometry, build orientation and support generation, and resource needs (cost and time). The 2020 version scores multi-criteria AM readiness with physical-programming preference functions.
NRE_note: The 2018 framework evaluates build orientation and support generation as a manufacturability perspective; whether redesign or build-preparation effort enters the readiness assessment cannot be confirmed from the abstracts (Ghiasian et al. 2018, 2020 abstracts).
Production_note: Economic feasibility is assessed, with 'resources necessary (i.e., cost and time)' as a feasibility perspective scored with preference functions, but the abstracts show no per-part cost build-up (Ghiasian et al. 2018, 2020 abstracts).
QA_Qual_note: Only abstracts are reachable and the 2020 multi-criteria readiness criteria are not listed, so whether certification is a criterion cannot be established (Ghiasian et al. 2020 abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only abstracts are reachable and the readiness criteria are not listed, so whether inspection or post-processing is assessed cannot be established (Ghiasian et al. 2020 abstract).
Storage_note: The documented scope is whether one component's design is ready for AM fabrication, which plainly excludes spares inventory (Ghiasian et al. 2020 abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The abstracts name resource cost and economic feasibility but do not show whether machine cost or multi-part builds enter it (Ghiasian et al. 2018, 2020 abstracts).
Shared_Capacity_note: A single-component design-readiness score; pooled print capacity across sites or users is plainly outside its documented scope (Ghiasian et al. 2020 abstract).
Speed_note: The 2018 framework assesses fabrication feasibility partly on 'resources necessary (i.e., cost and time)', so fabrication time is a feasibility criterion, but the abstracts do not show whether build or lead time is computed or reported (Ghiasian et al. 2018 abstract).

name: Mançanares et al. AHP AM process selection
developer: C. G. Mançanares, E. de S. Zancul, J. C. da Silva (University of São Paulo); P. A. Cauchick Miguel
description: Gathers parameters of the main commercial AM machines and uses AHP to rank the technologies and machines able to meet a part's technical specifications.
NRE_note: Only the abstract and a secondary review's summary were available (full text paywalled), and neither says whether design or engineering effort enters the AHP criteria (Springer abstract; SN Applied Sciences review Sec. 2.2).
Production_note: A later review describes the method's AHP criteria as including part cost alongside material variety and surface quality, with processes scored 'according to a database about each technology', so cost is a ranking criterion but not calculated (SN Applied Sciences 2019 review, Sec. 2.2).
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract and a secondary summary were available, and neither says whether material or process qualification is a criterion (Springer abstract; SN Applied Sciences review Sec. 2.2).
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract and a secondary summary were available; surface quality and precision are capability criteria, but neither source says whether inspection is considered (SN Applied Sciences review Sec. 2.2).
Storage_note: Outside the documented scope: the method ranks AM technologies and machines against one part's technical specifications, which does not involve inventory (USP and Springer abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: Only the abstract and a secondary summary were available; machine parameters are inputs, but neither says whether machine cost or utilisation is considered (Springer abstract; SN Applied Sciences review Sec. 2.2).
Shared_Capacity_note: Outside the documented scope: choosing a technology and machine for one part's specifications does not involve capacity pooled across sites or users (USP and Springer abstract).
Speed_note: Only the abstract and a secondary summary were available; no time criterion is listed, but build time is plausibly in scope for machine selection and the full text is unseen (SN Applied Sciences review Sec. 2.2).

name: Liu et al. SCOR-based aircraft spare parts AM model
developer: Peng Liu, Samuel H. Huang, Abhiram Mokasdar, Heng Zhou, Liang Hou (affiliations not verified)
description: Uses the SCOR reference model to compare conventional, centralized-AM and distributed-AM aircraft spare parts supply chains, quantifying safety-stock reduction from shorter AM lead times under heterogeneous demand.
NRE_note: Only secondary descriptions were read; Knofius (2018) says part design is treated as identical for AM and CM, which suggests no redesign cost, but digitisation or other one-time costs cannot be ruled out without the paywalled paper (Knofius 2018 thesis, ch. 1).
Production_note: Secondary descriptions cover inventory and lead-time effects only, and Knofius (2018) says AM equipment investment and personnel costs are omitted; whether any AM unit production cost is modelled is not shown (Knofius 2018; Mecheter et al. 2022; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).
QA_Qual_note: None of the secondary descriptions mentions qualification or certification, and the paywalled paper was not reached (Mecheter et al. 2022; Abidar & Chaabane 2022; Knofius 2018).
QA_Insp_note: None of the secondary descriptions mentions inspection or testing, and the paywalled paper was not reached (Mecheter et al. 2022; Abidar & Chaabane 2022; Knofius 2018).
Storage_note: The model derives required safety inventory at each distribution centre, service location and the OEM for conventional, centralised-AM and distributed-AM scenarios, showing reduced safety inventory and inventory-holding cost with AM (Mecheter et al. 2022 encyclopedia entry; Knofius 2018).
Shared_Capital_note: Knofius's review documents that the model's scope excludes AM equipment investment, biasing it toward decentralised deployment (Knofius 2018 thesis, ch. 1).
Shared_Capacity_note: The model compares central deployment of AM capacity, aggregating demand for slow movers, with deployment at service locations, a modelled site configuration, but no printer contention or queueing setting lead time is described (Knofius 2018; Mecheter et al. 2022).
Speed_note: Secondary descriptions show manufacturing and logistics lead times, with a cycle service-level target, entering the calculation of required safety inventory per configuration, but no source shows lead time, availability or downtime computed as an output (Mecheter et al. 2022 encyclopedia entry; Knofius 2018; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).

name: Li et al. system-dynamics comparison of conventional, centralized and distributed AM spare parts SCs
developer: Yao Li, Guozhu Jia, Yang Cheng, Yuchen Hu (Cheng: Aalborg University; others not verified)
description: System dynamics simulation comparing a conventional spare parts supply chain with centralized and distributed AM-based chains on total variable cost and carbon emissions; AM chains outperform on sustainability.
NRE_note: The abstract and secondary descriptions do not mention design or digitisation cost (Abidar & Chaabane list only transportation, manufacturing, administrative and inventory cost), and the paywalled full text was not reached (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022, Table 2).
Production_note: Manufacturing cost is one of the components of the simulated total variable cost compared across conventional and AM supply chains, but whether it is built from machine, material and labour inputs or entered as per-technology unit costs was not seen (Abidar & Chaabane 2022, Table 2; IDEAS abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Neither the abstract nor the secondary descriptions mention qualification, and the full text was not reached (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).
QA_Insp_note: Neither the abstract nor the secondary descriptions mention inspection, and the full text was not reached (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).
Storage_note: A literature table lists inventory cost, under make-to-inventory, among the components of the total variable cost that the system-dynamics model compares across conventional, centralised-AM and distributed-AM chains, so AM's effect on inventory cost is computed, though this rests on one cell of a preprint's table rather than the paper (Abidar & Chaabane 2022, Table 2).
Shared_Capital_note: Neither the abstract nor the secondary cost-component list mentions AM machine capital or its sharing; reading 'total variable cost' as excluding capital would be inference (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).
Shared_Capacity_note: The simulation models AM site configuration, comparing one centralised AM-based chain with a distributed AM-based chain on cost and emissions, but no capacity contention or effect on lead time is reported (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).
Speed_note: The abstract and the secondary descriptions mention no lead time, backorder or downtime measure; outputs reported are total variable cost and carbon emission (IDEAS abstract; Abidar & Chaabane 2022).

name: Song-Zhang 'Stock or Print' multi-part printer queue model
developer: Jing-Sheng Song (Duke University, Fuqua), Yue Zhang (Pennsylvania State University, Smeal)
decision_levels: Part selection; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Decides which of many parts to stock under (r,q) policies and which to print on demand on a shared printer modeled as a multiclass queue, minimizing long-run average system cost. Optimal printer utilization is low, yet savings are significant; stocking and printing are complements.
NRE_note: Only the abstract and press summaries are public and they do not mention design, digitisation or setup cost (EconPapers abstract; Duke Fuqua Insights).
Production_note: Printing enters as an 'additional unit cost of printing' premium parameter against stocking, a lumped AM unit cost with no geometry, material or machine build-up (EconPapers abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract and press summaries are public and they do not mention qualification or part quality (EconPapers abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract and press summaries are public and they do not mention inspection (EconPapers abstract).
Storage_note: The model decides which parts to stock under (r,q) policies and which to print on demand within a minimised long-run average cost, so AM's effect on stock is computed (EconPapers abstract and keywords; Duke Fuqua Insights).
Shared_Capital_note: The abstract shows one printer serving many part types and reports its optimal utilisation, but does not say whether printer purchase or fixed cost is in the objective (EconPapers abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: Many part types share one printer modelled as a multiclass queue, and optimal utilisation rises with part variety and falls with part criticality, so contention for the printer sets service; this is one firm's printer with no cross-site pooling (EconPapers abstract and keywords).
Speed_note: The queue model makes printed parts wait for the printer, printing speed is a parameter with S-shaped savings, and part criticality shifts parts back to stock, so delay enters the minimised system cost, although the exact delay-penalty form was not seen (EconPapers abstract; Duke Fuqua Insights).

name: Westerweel lifecycle-cost model for AM vs traditional component design
developer: Bram Westerweel, Rob J.I. Basten, Geert-Jan van Houtum (Eindhoven University of Technology)
description: Lifecycle cost comparison including technology-specific one-time design investment, production cost and lead time, reliability-driven maintenance and downtime, and performance benefits; derives break-even reliability/cost conditions for the AM part.
NRE_note: A technology-specific one-time design investment is an explicit term of the lifecycle cost model, and the paper analyses when performance benefits outweigh AM design costs (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).
Production_note: Unit production cost is an explicit input for each technology (AM vs traditional) in the lifecycle cost comparison, with break-even conditions derived, which meets the per-technology unit-cost input test (IDEAS/RePEc abstract; Westerweel WP2 deck, 'Unit production costs').
QA_Qual_note: The abstract says the two designs differ in reliability but does not show whether qualification effort or cost is modelled, and no full text is open (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract is public and it does not mention inspection or testing (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).
Storage_note: The abstract says the short AM lead time can lower 'after-sales logistics costs' but does not say these are inventory or holding costs, so whether stock is modelled cannot be settled (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: Only the abstract is public and it does not mention AM machine capital or its allocation (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: The abstract does not mention AM capacity, and the author's deck lists on-site AM capacity only as a separate research topic (IDEAS/RePEc abstract; Westerweel WP2 deck).
Speed_note: Maintenance and downtime costs are explicit lifecycle cost components and production lead time differs by technology, so downtime is costed in the comparison (IDEAS/RePEc abstract).

name: Zhang-Westerweel-Basten-Song IP licensing / distributed printing model
developer: Yue Zhang, Bram Westerweel, Rob Basten, Jing-Sheng Song (Eindhoven University of Technology; Duke University)
description: Game-theoretic model of an OEM choosing license terms when buyers can switch from centralized physical supply to local printing via a third-party provider with shorter lead times and lower setup costs; price competitiveness of printing drives decentralization.
NRE_note: Only the abstract and seminar summaries could be read; they describe the OEM selling designs under licence but not whether design or digitisation cost is modelled (Penn State Pure abstract; Fudan seminar page).
Production_note: Printing price and setup cost are model parameters (results turn on 3D printing's price competitiveness, explored in numerical experiments), but the abstract shows no per-part cost build-up (Penn State Pure abstract).
QA_Qual_note: The abstract and seminar summaries do not mention qualification or part quality, and the full text was not available, so whether it is modelled cannot be established (Penn State Pure abstract; Fudan seminar page).
QA_Insp_note: The abstract and keywords do not mention inspection, and the full text was not available (Penn State Pure abstract).
Storage_note: The abstract models lead time and setup cost across centralized and local-printing channels and inventory appears only in keywords and framing; whether inventory enters the model cannot be confirmed from public sources (Penn State Pure abstract; IDEAS/RePEc keywords).
Shared_Capital_note: The abstract describes buyers printing through a third-party provider but does not show whether provider printer capital or its spreading across buyers is modelled (Penn State Pure abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: The abstract and seminar summary do not mention provider capacity or contention among buyers, so whether it is modelled cannot be established (Penn State Pure abstract; Fudan seminar page).
Speed_note: The shorter lead time of local printing is a channel parameter that drives each buyer's channel choice and the OEM's optimal licence, but the abstract does not show lead time being valued or reported as an output (Penn State Pure abstract; Fudan seminar page).

name: Knofius et al. (2021) AM/CM dual-sourcing spare parts MDP (OR Spectrum)
developer: Nils Knofius, Matthieu van der Heijden, Andrei Sleptchenko, Henk Zijm (University of Twente; Sleptchenko: Khalifa University)
earlier_versions: Knofius, van der Heijden, Sleptchenko & Zijm (2017), BETA Working Paper 530 'Improving effectiveness of spare part supply by additive manufacturing as dual sourcing option': pre-publication version of the same model.
description: Continuous-time Markov decision model (solved by LP) choosing at each failure which version (AM or CM) to install and which to reorder, plus base stock, where AM and CM parts have different failure rates. Dual sourcing saves ~8% on average (up to >30%) vs best single source; AM mainly serves as emergency source.
NRE_note: Additional AM design cost is an explicit cost term, depreciated over the remaining life cycle as d per time unit and, though kept outside the MDP itself, applied to the reported cost savings of dual sourcing with a sensitivity analysis and a case value (EUR 15,000 design cost, d = EUR 1,000/yr) (Knofius et al. 2021, secs. 3.3, 3.7, 4.2, 5).
Production_note: Explicit per-part unit costs by technology, AM piece price c_A and CM piece price c_C, are model inputs entering the purchasing cost term (case: c_A = EUR 1,197, c_C = EUR 480), though they are not built up from machine time or material (Knofius et al. 2021, Table 1, secs. 3.3, 5).
QA_Qual_note: Certification is discussed as a barrier, with a case estimate of about EUR 250,000 that 'renders any application of AM economically infeasible', but this figure is excluded from the model and from the Fig. 10 cost comparison, so it does not affect the sourcing decision (Knofius et al. 2021, sec. 5).
QA_Insp_note: Full paper read; per-part inspection or testing is not parameterised or modelled, quality checks appearing only in the introduction as a general AM cost disadvantage (Knofius et al. 2021, secs. 1, 3, 4.1).
Storage_note: Holding cost is a fraction of unit cost of stocked items and base stock S is optimised, so AM's effect on stock is quantified (e.g., average AM base stock 1.31 at one-week AM lead time; case holding costs EUR 752/507/534) (Knofius et al. 2021, secs. 3.2, 3.5, 4.2, 5).
Shared_Capital_note: Full paper read; printer capital is not modelled and expensive AM equipment is cited only as the reason to assume an external supplier, with no description of machine cost being spread across parts or users (Knofius et al. 2021, secs. 2.3, 3.1).
Shared_Capacity_note: The AM supplier's capacity is described as shared between multiple customers but assumed uncapacitated, with gross throughput time a fixed input, so the model neither routes work nor models contention (Knofius et al. 2021, sec. 3.1, assumption 4).
Speed_note: The model computes backorders with a backorder (downtime) cost b per item per time unit (case EUR 15,000-50,000/day) and AM and CM resupply lead times drive the optimal policy (Knofius et al. 2021, secs. 3.2, 3.3, 5).

name: Knofius AM part-consolidation METRIC lifecycle model
developer: Nils Knofius, Matthieu van der Heijden, Henk Zijm (University of Twente)
description: Multi-indenture METRIC-based model of total cost (logistics, manufacturing, repair) of consolidated AM parts vs conventional assemblies; consolidation often raises total cost because a failure forces replacement of the whole part, and shorter AM lead times barely offset this.
NRE_note: The 'Development and Production Costs' subsection says AM needs less tooling, setup and design preparation and that the authors 'encapsulate these considerations with the difference in unit costs', while fixed costs are not regarded explicitly, so the model has no NRE term and NRE does not drive any decision (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.3.1).
Production_note: Piece prices are per-part inputs, but the consolidated AM part's price is set as a ratio to the conventional price and varied, a lumped AM premium with no build-up (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.3.1, 3.4.4, 3.5.1).
QA_Qual_note: Standardisation and qualification are named as major AM adoption challenges that contribute to the high AM piece price, which the authors 'encapsulate' in the unit-cost difference, but no qualification term enters the model or any decision (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.3.1).
QA_Insp_note: Quality checks for repaired items and quality-driven post-processing or rework of AM parts are named in the cost discussion, but inspection is not a model term or input and does not enter the consolidation decision (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.3.1-3.3.2).
Storage_note: Base-stock levels are optimised under an availability target and holding cost (0.15 or 0.3 of piece price) is computed on stock, so the effect of consolidation and AM lead time on inventory is quantified (Knofius thesis, Eqs. 3.1, 3.5, Sec. 3.5.1).
Shared_Capital_note: The thesis explains that AM machinery is an expensive, risky investment and that low in-house utilisation across many items raises piece prices, discussion that does not enter the model as a capital or utilisation term (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.3.1).
Shared_Capacity_note: The model assumes unconstrained repair capacity with contracted lead times at a single stock point, so capacity is outside its documented scope (Knofius thesis, Sec. 3.4.3, Assumption 10).
Speed_note: Expected backorders and system availability (1 - EBO/installed base) are computed with VARI-METRIC for each configuration under an availability constraint, with AM lead time varied as a factor of the conventional lead time (Knofius thesis, Eqs. 3.1, 3.4, Sec. 3.5.1).

name: Cantini spare parts supply chain configuration DSS (AM vs CM, degree of centralization)
developer: Alessandra Cantini, Filippo De Carlo (University of Florence); Mirco Peron, Fabio Sgarbossa (NTNU)
description: Cost model (purchasing, ordering, holding, transport, backorders) over five degrees of stock centralization x AM/CM, run over 10,000 Sobol scenarios and distilled into a decision tree (77% accuracy at depth 4, 97% at depth 15); hybrid centralization most often optimal.
NRE_note: Digitising AM items is only stated as included in the supplier's unit price and is never a separate input or varied, so NRE does not act in the configuration decision (UNIFI FLORE full text, Sec. 3, Assumption 2).
Production_note: Per-technology unit purchasing costs are explicit model inputs (ucAM 100-2,500 EUR, ucCM 10-2,500 EUR; Case A CM 1,057 vs AM 1,370 EUR) entering purchasing and holding cost (UNIFI FLORE full text, Eq. 4, Tables 2-3).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification or certification is not addressed in the model or text (UNIFI FLORE full text).
QA_Insp_note: Quality control is only stated as part of the supplier's cost inside the unit price and AM's longer inspection times are discussed, but inspection is never a separate input and does not act in the decision (UNIFI FLORE full text, Assumption 2, Sec. 2.2).
Storage_note: Holding cost is computed per DC from average inventory (Q/2 plus Poisson safety stock over each technology's lead time) times unit cost and a 25% rate, times the number of DCs (UNIFI FLORE full text, Eqs. 11-15).
Shared_Capital_note: Only variable costs are modelled with no investment in facilities or assets, equipment fixed costs sit inside the supplier price, and AM printer fixed costs are left to future work (UNIFI FLORE full text, Assumption 9, Sec. 5.2).
Shared_Capacity_note: A single external supplier with no capacity constraints is assumed, and the degree of centralisation pools stock across DCs rather than print capacity (UNIFI FLORE full text, Assumptions 1 and 3, Eq. 1).
Speed_note: Expected backorders are computed per configuration and costed at 1,000-100,000 EUR per backorder, with AM lead times of 1-4 weeks vs CM 4-26 weeks (UNIFI FLORE full text, Eqs. 19-20, Table 2).

name: Heinen-Hoberg portfolio-level AM switchover model
developer: J. Jakob Heinen, Kai Hoberg (Kuehne Logistics University, Hamburg)
description: Inventory-model-based portfolio analysis of which SKUs become cheaper to supply with AM given demand, TM fixed costs and minimum order quantities; at a 300% AM premium ~8% of SKUs (2% of units) switch, cutting system cost ~6.4%.
NRE_note: The developers' release says AM requires certain investments, for example in technical drawings, but whether drawing creation is a cost term the model uses cannot be confirmed from the abstract and release (KLU press release via idw; vLex record).
Production_note: AM unit production cost enters as a premium multiple of TM cost (up to four times, a 300% premium) with no part-level build-up (vLex abstract and Sec. 1).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification is not mentioned in the abstract, the visible pp. 810-812 or the press release, and the model sections are paywalled (vLex record).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection is not mentioned in the abstract, the visible pages or the press release, and the model sections are paywalled (vLex record).
Storage_note: The inventory-model-based analysis computes optimal stock quantities and supply chain cost per SKU under TM fixed costs and minimum order quantities versus AM, reporting a 6.4% system-cost cut; the holding-cost formulation itself is paywalled (vLex abstract and Sec. 1; KLU press release).
Shared_Capital_note: The release mentions hardware investment for AM, but neither it nor the visible pages show machine capital being spread or shared, and the model sections are paywalled (KLU press release; vLex record).
Shared_Capacity_note: AM capacity, sites or network placement are not mentioned in the abstract, visible pages or release, and the model sections are paywalled (vLex record).
Speed_note: The developers' release lists service level as a model factor and delivery time among the parameters the model calculates, but the model sections are paywalled, so whether lead time or backorders are computed is not verified (KLU press release; vLex Sec. 1).

name: Cokyasar-Jin AM capacity allocation problem (AMCAP) over a network
developer: Taner Cokyasar, Mingzhou Jin
decision_levels: Part selection; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Mixed-integer nonlinear program assigning each part to on-demand AM at a facility or an alternative source (e.g., inventory), sizing AM capacity, with convex nonlinear waiting time at each AM facility; optimal deployment saves ~20% vs no AM.
NRE_note: The abstract lists production, transportation, alternative sourcing and lead-time costs but no design or one-time cost, and the closed full text and the authors' code repository could not be read (Tarsus abstract).
Production_note: Production cost is a minimised objective term with machine cost and build speed as parameters, but how per-part AM cost is built up is not visible (Tarsus abstract).
QA_Qual_note: The abstract does not mention qualification and the full text is closed (Tarsus abstract).
QA_Insp_note: The abstract does not mention inspection and the full text is closed (Tarsus abstract).
Storage_note: The cost of the alternative sourcing option, exemplified by inventory holding, is a minimised objective term for parts not assigned to AM, but whether it is a holding-cost formulation on stock levels is not visible (Tarsus abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The number of AM machines per facility is a decision traded off against machine cost and the volume of parts assigned to AM, with sensitivity on machine cost and build speed (Tarsus abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: Parts assigned to each AM facility in the network share its capacity, and a convex nonlinear waiting time at each facility feeds lead-time cost, so contention sets lead time (Tarsus abstract).
Speed_note: Lead-time cost, driven by waiting time at AM facilities, is an explicit minimised objective term (Tarsus abstract).

name: Veitenheimer AFIT centralized vs distributed AM Monte Carlo (EOD robots)
developer: Capt Shane R. Veitenheimer, USAF (Air Force Institute of Technology)
description: Excel/VBA Monte Carlo (10,000 trials) of repair-part costs and intratheater shipping under centralized (Bagram depot) vs distributed AM, converting annual savings to NPV over 3-10 year machine lives to back-solve the justifiable printer price (~$72.8k-232.7k centralized/full down to ~$520-1,690 distributed/limited).
NRE_note: Design cost is not modelled; the conclusions only discuss covering design investment through technical-data provisions in a large acquisition contract (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. V).
Production_note: The model simulates existing work-order repair-part costs as the cost AM would avoid and assumes the machine takes 65% of AM investment, a lumped ratio; AM material, print time and labour are not built up (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III-IV).
QA_Qual_note: Testing against standards is discussed as a barrier in the background, and the limited-AM scenarios exclude cloth and electronic parts as a scope choice, so qualification does not enter the model (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. I and III).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection and testing of parts are absent from the cost model; the only quality content is a cited comparison of gear strength between two machines (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III and V).
Storage_note: Inventory carrying and obsolescence costs are explicitly excluded as ill-defined and assumed unchanged (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III).
Shared_Capital_note: Annual savings are converted by annuity NPV over 3-10 year machine lives into a justifiable machine price for one central machine at Bagram versus one per squadron site (full AM $112k-358k central vs $26k-85k per site), trading machine count against scale (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III-IV, Tables 13-14).
Shared_Capacity_note: Centralized (one depot) and distributed (squadron-level) configurations are modelled with intratheater air shipping costs, but no printer capacity, queue or lead-time effect is included (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III).
Speed_note: Downtime is explicitly excluded and lead time and build time are not modelled; the thesis says it placed less emphasis on AM time savings (Veitenheimer 2017, Ch. III and V).

name: NPS data-farming simulations of expeditionary AM logistics and Ao (NPS-LM-22-006, 2022)
developer: Susan M. Sanchez, Claudia Luhrs, Mary L. McDonald, Maj Greg Lynch USMC (Naval Postgraduate School, Acquisition Research Program)
earlier_versions: Sanchez, Lynch, Luhrs & McDonald (2019) 'Networked Logistics and Additive Manufacturing', Acquisition Research Symposium slides SYM-AM-19-156: earlier presentation of the data-farmed 'Iron Network' AM simulation; the 2022 report is the full write-up and includes the operational availability model.
description: Discrete-event simulations with nearly-orthogonal Latin hypercube data farming: AM factors had small effects on network delivery performance, but in the Ao model (notional data) AM parts raised days with >=42 operational vehicles from 13% to 79% with fewer maintainers and vehicles.
NRE_note: The full report's factors (Tables 2 and 3) cover AM demand shares, reliability, self-supply and repair-time multipliers only; design files, digitisation or parameter development are not modelled or discussed (NPS-LM-22-006).
Production_note: No cost parameters are modelled; cost appears only in qualitative discussion of private-sector AM adoption (NPS-LM-22-006).
QA_Qual_note: AM part suitability is discussed as a barrier by part class and an AM reliability multiplier (0.5-2.0) varies part life, but qualification itself does not enter the simulation (NPS-LM-22-006 Sec. 5, pp. 30-31; Table 3).
QA_Insp_note: The conclusions recommend statistical quality control or other quality assurance for AM parts, and inspection does not enter the simulation (NPS-LM-22-006 Sec. 5, p. 30).
Storage_note: AM is discussed as reducing storage by keeping bulk raw materials instead of spare-part stockpiles, but the Ao model holds no inventory and storage enters no decision (NPS-LM-22-006 Sec. 2.3, 3.1).
Shared_Capital_note: Printer investment, equipment amortisation or sharing are not modelled; equipment cost appears only in a passing liability remark about using external manufacturers when training or specialty equipment costs are high (NPS-LM-22-006 p. 31).
Shared_Capacity_note: Seabase, logistics nodes and supported units are named as candidate AM placements, but AM enters the network model only as a demand adjustment, with no AM sites, routing of requests or printer capacity (NPS-LM-22-006 Sec. 3.1-3.2).
Speed_note: The simulations compute operational availability (days with at least 42 vehicles mission capable: 13% regular parts vs 79% with AM; annual readiness 6% vs 64%) and request turnaround time (1.6-2.8 days) (NPS-LM-22-006 Sec. 4.1-4.2).

name: NPS KVA / real-options make-or-buy model for Navy ship parts (3DP + 3D scanning + CPLM)
developer: David Ford (Texas A&M); Tom Housel, Sandra Hom, Johnathan Mun (Naval Postgraduate School)
description: Knowledge Value Added ROI, Monte Carlo volatility and real options compare make/buy mixes by part complexity; all-Navy production estimated to save ~$12.7M/yr per depot (~$120M across 10 depots), with a phased compound option most valuable.
NRE_note: 3D laser scanning is one of the three technologies valued and design changes are named as a cost driver, but no scanning, reverse-engineering or redesign effort enters the KVA or real-options calculation (Ford et al. 2015 pp. 183, 186-187).
Production_note: Costs are back-derived as Cost = Benefits/(ROI+1) from assumed average part values by complexity ($1k/$3k/$6k) and KVA ROI with Navy labour rates, summed over six industry/Navy complexity classes, with no geometry, material or machine build-up (Ford et al. 2015 pp. 189-191).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification, certification and first-article testing are not addressed anywhere in the paper (Ford et al. 2015).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection and testing are not addressed in the KVA or real-options models (Ford et al. 2015).
Storage_note: Inventory and storage are not addressed; the model compares make/buy cost and ROI only (Ford et al. 2015).
Shared_Capital_note: Real options value phased investment in the technologies (25/50/75/100% with exit after small-scale investment), but phasing does not spread machine cost across parts or users and no machine capital cost, amortisation or utilisation is entered (Ford et al. 2015 pp. 192-193).
Shared_Capacity_note: The model rests on one depot making about 27,000 parts a year and multiplies savings by 10 depots; printer capacity, pooling or contention are not modelled (Ford et al. 2015 pp. 189, 192).
Speed_note: Shorter in-sourced cycle times are linked to fleet readiness as motivation in the abstract and introduction, but no cycle-time, lead-time or readiness figure enters the model (Ford et al. 2015 pp. 182-184).

name: Jedeck spare-parts-on-demand AM vs warehousing simulation (Arena)
developer: Stefan Jedeck (University of Louisville)
decision_levels: Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Arena discrete-event simulation routing each request through parallel warehousing and AM paths to compare costs under varied build speed, build volume, material price, machine price, cool-down, and multi-machine/multi-material strategies.
NRE_note: The dissertation assumes all pre-work (engineering, CAD data) is already done, so no design, file-preparation or parameter cost is modelled (Jedeck 2015, ch. 3).
Production_note: Per-part AM cost is built from material consumption x price (EUR 80/kg base), operator cost per part, machine purchase price and depreciation, maintenance, training and energy, with build speed and build volume setting run time (Jedeck 2015, Table 3-3 and ch. 3).
QA_Qual_note: The full dissertation does not mention qualification or certification of parts, materials or processes; validation refers only to the simulation model (Jedeck 2015, full text).
QA_Insp_note: No part inspection or testing is modelled; rework (cleaning as the standard step) appears only as extra process time, and 'inspections' refer to equipment maintenance (Jedeck 2015, ch. 3 and 8).
Storage_note: The warehouse route computes storage cost as total stock value times a storage-cost rate, with EOQ and reorder points per part, so holding cost is compared with the AM-on-demand route (Jedeck 2015, sections 3.4.6, 5.1 and Table 3-3).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine purchase price is depreciated over time and spread across all requests served, batches fill the build volume, utilisation is an output, and one-, two- and three-machine strategies are compared (Jedeck 2015, Table 3-3, ch. 5 and 7).
Shared_Capacity_note: Requests queue by priority for batches on a shared AM site, so utilisation and queueing set delivery time and late penalties (penalties rise sharply near 38-39% utilisation); single site with 1-3 machines, no cross-site pooling (Jedeck 2015, ch. 3, 5 and 7).
Speed_note: Time from request to delivery is simulated and delivery beyond a part's allowed time (48/72/192 h) incurs a penalty cost, as does a warehouse stock-out (Jedeck 2015, Table 3-3 and ch. 4).

name: O'Brien aerospace spare parts AM shop DES vs warehouse model
developer: Kyle O'Brien (University of Louisville)
description: Discrete-event simulation of AM machines and operators benchmarked against an inventory-theory warehouse model; AM saves money when late-delivery penalties are high, and adding machines beats adding operators.
NRE_note: Per-order time for receiving orders and manipulating the CAD file for AM is costed through operator time, but no one-time redesign or reverse-engineering cost is modelled (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.A.2).
Production_note: Per-part AM cost is computed in the simulation from operator time ($70/h), machine purchase and maintenance, material at $0.2/g using Ti-6Al-4V density, energy at $0.02/kWh and post-processing time (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.C, V.B, Table 7).
QA_Qual_note: FAA certification under high process variability is discussed as a barrier for aerospace AM spares, but qualification is not used in the simulation (O'Brien 2020, sec. II.A).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection is folded into the post-processing step: the operator performs a quality check on each batch within a triangular post-processing time (0.08-1.2 h per part) charged at operator rate, with no separate inspection cost (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.A.2, App. III).
Storage_note: The benchmark warehouse model computes safety stock from service-level z-score and demand variability, with holding cost at 10% of part value and reorder-point purchasing (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.B.1, Eqs. 1-4).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine purchase ($1,000,000 each) and maintenance enter the cost model with depreciation tracked, and one- versus two-machine configurations are traded off against demand rate, a second machine paying off only at the highest demand (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.C, V.B, App. III).
Shared_Capacity_note: Orders contend for shared machine and operator capacity in one AM shop, so queues, utilisation and re-sequencing set lead time and penalties; there is no cross-site pooling (O'Brien 2020, sec. IV.C, V.B, VI).
Speed_note: The simulation outputs lead time and charges a prorated late-delivery penalty for hours beyond each order's allocated due date (O'Brien 2020, abstract, Table 7, sec. IV.E, V.A).

name: Abidar-Chaabane METRIC model with centralized/decentralized AM repair
developer: Youssef Abidar, Amin Chaabane (Ecole de technologie superieure, Montreal)
description: METRIC scenarios with AM at the central centre vs at regional centres, varying AM repair time and probability by demand class; decentralized AM best when AM is faster, or equally fast with >70% AM repair probability; slow/non-moving parts most suitable.
NRE_note: No design, digitisation or engineering cost appears in the full preprint; the only cost input is item unit price (Research Square preprint, Table 3, Appendices A-C).
Production_note: AM repair or production cost is not an input or output; AM enters only through repair time and repair probability, and unit price only dollarises backorders (Research Square preprint, Sec. 5.1, Appendices A-B).
QA_Qual_note: Qualification or certification of AM repairs is not modelled or discussed in the full preprint (Research Square preprint).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection or testing of AM-repaired parts is not modelled or discussed (Research Square preprint).
Storage_note: Stock levels at central and regional centres are inputs to the METRIC backorder calculation under each AM scenario, but no holding cost or inventory investment is output (Research Square preprint, Sec. 4.2, Tables 4 and 6).
Shared_Capital_note: The final phase uses backorder results to argue for AM investment, contrasting one central AM site with machines at each regional centre, but machine or investment cost appears in no equation or table and does not enter the comparison (Research Square preprint, Sec. 3, Appendix B, Conclusion).
Shared_Capacity_note: AM placement (one central site serving both regions vs AM at each regional centre) is modelled and its effect on expected backorders computed, but AM capacity is not modelled (high repair capacity is assumed), so contention does not set service (Research Square preprint, Sec. 4.1, Appendices A-B).
Speed_note: Expected backorders are computed per AM placement, repair-time and repair-probability scenario and converted to dollars via unit price (Research Square preprint, Eq. 3, Table 5, Appendix C).

name: ISO/ASTM 52967:2024 part classifications for AM parts used in aviation
developer: ASTM Committee F42 / ISO TC 261 (joint)
earlier_versions: ASTM F3572-22 (2022): original ASTM practice with the same four consequence-of-failure classes (A-D); still listed as active by ASTM; published as joint ISO/ASTM 52967 in 2024 (valid from Oct 2024).
description: Assigns aviation AM parts to Class A (high), B (medium), C (low) or D (negligible) by consequence of failure. The class is meant as a common metric that downstream material, process, NDI and qualification specifications use to set levels of process control, post-processing, qualification and inspection.
NRE_note: The practice only assigns consequence-of-failure classes and is 'not intended to establish criteria for any downstream processes', so one-time engineering cost is plainly outside its scope (ASTM F3572-22 sample, 1.4).
Production_note: A classification practice; per-part cost is plainly outside its scope and cost is not mentioned in the visible text (ASTM F3572-22 sample, sec. 1).
QA_Qual_note: The four classes are a consequence-of-failure metric meant to set 'appropriate levels of process control, thermal post processing, qualification, and inspection' in downstream specifications, but the practice itself prescribes no qualification activities for any class (ASTM F3572-22 sample, Introduction, 1.4-1.5).
QA_Insp_note: The class is offered as a metric for downstream non-destructive inspection and testing processes, but the practice prescribes no inspection scope for any class (ASTM F3572-22 sample, 1.5; ASTM store scope).
Storage_note: A part-classification practice; inventory is plainly outside its scope and not mentioned in the visible text (ASTM F3572-22 sample).
Shared_Capital_note: A part-classification practice; equipment cost or sharing is plainly outside its scope, and a common class metric is not reuse of qualification across parts (ASTM F3572-22 sample, 1.6).
Shared_Capacity_note: A part-classification practice; print capacity is plainly outside its scope (ASTM F3572-22 sample).
Speed_note: A part-classification practice; lead time is plainly outside its scope and not mentioned in the visible text (ASTM F3572-22 sample).

name: Joint Additive Manufacturing Acceptability (JAMA) framework, Phase II
year: Unknown (NCMS announcement undated; page last modified 22 Oct 2024)
developer: U.S. Air Force with NCMS (CTMA program), industry and academia
